definition_en: a written plan of action, a list or show, or a set of coded instructions; to arrange or write such instructions
core_image: 墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器照着纸条上的指令一行行运行

sceneCN: 这里 program 指交给计算机执行的一整套指令（第 4 个义项：计算机程序）；句意：工程师载入程序，看着机器逐行执行。图中可辨识物件：墙上的时间表、纸条、旧机器、指示灯；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A plan of future action
senses.definition: a set of intended actions arranged in advance to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个目标而事先安排好的一系列行动
senses.example: The city launched a housing program for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府启动了一项面向低收入家庭的住房计划。
senses.why: the Greek noun began as a public notice written down ahead of time, so the word still carries the idea of something laid out before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词最初指事先写好的公开通告，因此这个词始终带着「事情发生之前就摆好的安排」这一层意思。

senses.title: An order of events
senses.definition: a list showing the times and order of the parts of an event
senses.definitionCN: 列出活动各部分时间与顺序的清单
senses.example: The conference program lists every talk and the room it uses.
senses.exampleCN: 会议日程列出了每场报告及其所在房间。
senses.why: a written notice of what will happen and when is the most literal survival of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「将发生什么、何时发生」写下来通告，正是原义最直接的延续。

senses.title: A printed list for an audience
senses.definition: the printed sheet given to an audience, naming the performers and the works
senses.definitionCN: 发给观众、写明演出者与曲目的印刷纸页
senses.example: She read the program before the orchestra tuned up.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团调音之前，她先读了节目单。
senses.why: theatres turned the order of a performance into a small printed booklet, and the booklet took the name of the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 剧院把演出顺序做成一本小册子，册子便直接沿用了「顺序」这个名字。

senses.title: A show that is broadcast
senses.definition: a single show or an ongoing series carried by a station
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台播出的单个节目或系列节目
senses.example: The station dropped the program after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 电视台播出一季后停掉了这个节目。
senses.why: broadcasting inherited the word from theatre: each slot in the schedule is a program, whether or not paper is involved.
senses.whyCN: 广播沿用了剧院的说法：节目表上的每一个时段都叫一个节目，与纸张已无关系。

senses.title: Instructions a computer follows
senses.definition: an ordered set of coded instructions that makes a computer carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 使计算机完成一项任务的有序编码指令集合
senses.example: The program sorts the files by date and deletes the copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序按日期排序文件并删除重复副本。
senses.why: the earliest electronic machines were fed a written sequence of steps, exactly like a plan handed to a reader, so the plan word moved onto the machine.
senses.whyCN: 最早的电子机器接收的是一份写好的步骤序列，就像交给读者的一份计划，于是「计划」这个词就移到了机器上。

senses.title: A course of study
senses.definition: an organized course or set of courses leading to a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种资格的有组织课程或课程组合
senses.example: The new program leads to a master's degree in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新课程两年后可获硕士学位。
senses.why: schools borrowed the plan word because a degree is also a sequence of steps that a student is expected to complete in order.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了「计划」这个词，因为拿学位同样是一串要求学生按顺序完成的步骤。

senses.title: A government or agency scheme
senses.definition: an official scheme that organizes money and staff for a public purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为公共目的组织资金与人员的官方方案
senses.example: The literacy program trained teachers in three rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫盲计划在三个农村县培训了教师。
senses.why: public bodies write down what they intend to do and fund it, and that funded intention is called a program.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构把打算做的事写下来并拨款，这份带钱的打算就被称为项目。

senses.title: To set something to happen
senses.definition: to arrange for a device or system to act at a set time or in a set way
senses.definitionCN: 安排某个设备或系统在固定时间或以固定方式动作
senses.example: They programmed the lights to switch off at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯设定在午夜自动关闭。
senses.why: once a machine can hold its own sequence of steps, the verb means putting that sequence into it, even when no code is written by hand.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机器能自己保存步骤序列，动词就表示把序列装进去，哪怕并没有手写代码。

senses.title: To write instructions for a machine
senses.definition: to write the code that a computer or machine will execute
senses.definitionCN: 编写计算机或机器将要执行的代码
senses.example: He programmed the robot to pick only the ripe fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他给机器人编程，让它只摘成熟的果子。
senses.why: this is the modern verb built directly on the computing noun: the programmer writes the plan the machine will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由计算机义名词转来的现代动词：程序员写下机器将要遵循的计划。

intro.en: Program is Greek in origin, Latin in transmission and French in form. Its oldest sense is a public notice written in advance; the computing sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: program 源于希腊语，经拉丁语传递，形式取自法语。它最古老的意思是事先写好的公开通告；计算机义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek programma meant a public written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write. The noun named a posted announcement, not a scheme of action.
items.cn: 希腊语 programma 指公开的书面通告，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。这个名词指的是张贴出来的公告，而不是行动计划。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma as a learned noun for a written notice or preface, keeping the Greek shape and the written, public flavour.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 programma 作为书面通告或序言的学术名词，保留了希腊语的形式与「书面、公开」的色彩。

items.en: French programme entered English in the seventeenth century. English first used it for a public notice and soon for the printed order of a ceremony or performance.
items.cn: 法语 programme 在十七世纪进入英语。英语先用它指公开通告，很快又用它指仪式或演出的印刷顺序。

items.en: American printers shortened the ending to program. The two spellings now divide mainly by region, and the short form became standard in computing.
items.cn: 美国印刷者把词尾缩短为 program。两种拼写如今基本按地区分工，而短形式在计算机领域成为标准。

items.en: From the 1940s a program meant the coded sequence that drives a machine. The noun, and then the verb to program, followed the hardware into ordinary use.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，program 指驱动机器的编码序列。名词以及后来的动词「编程」随硬件一起进入日常使用。

items.en: The chain from Greek programma through Latin programma and French programme to English program is documented. Only the first written dates in English are approximate, and any Indo-European root proposed for graphein is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从希腊语 programma 经拉丁语 programma、法语 programme 到英语的这条链有文献依据，只是英语最早书证的年代为约数；为 graphein 提出的印欧语词根属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

note.en: The first group is the same word in other shapes and roles; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a plan, a timetable and software.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的其他形式与角色；第二组是与计划、时间表和软件相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, and the usual form for a printed list of performances; computing writing prefers program everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，也是节目单的常用形式；计算机写作各地多用 program。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code, not the code of one task; the noun names the work, while program names the product.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码这项活动，而不是某一任务的代码；名词指工作，program 指成品。

entries.definition: The person who writes the code; it answers who, where program answers what.
entries.definitionCN: 指写代码的人；它回答「谁」，而 program 回答「什么」。

entries.definition: Built on the Greek noun with a Latinised ending: it describes something done by fixed plan, as in programmatic music or programmatic reform.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊名词加拉丁化词尾构成：描述按固定计划进行的事物，如标题音乐或按纲领推行的改革。

entries.definition: The broad intention and the steps meant to reach it; a program is usually a plan that has been written down, funded or scheduled.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体意图及实现它的步骤；program 通常是已写下来、已拨款或已排期的计划。

entries.definition: The arrangement of times and dates; a program may contain a schedule, but a schedule says only when, not what for.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间与日期的安排；program 里可能含 schedule，但时间表只说「何时」，不说「为何」。

entries.definition: Programs and data treated as a product or a body of material; one program is a single unit of software.
entries.definitionCN: 把程序与数据当作产品与整套材料；一个 program 是软件的一个单元。

entries.definition: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting; it is a program for a discussion rather than for a machine or a season.
entries.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单；它是讨论的程序，而非机器或演出季的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek pro- means before and graphein means write, so a program is something written down before it happens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，graphein 意为「书写」，所以 program 就是事先写下来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs program, programme, programming, programmer, programmable and programmatic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programme、programming、programmer、programmable 与 programmatic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the plan sense: training program, welfare program, housing program.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「计划」义：培训计划、福利计划、住房计划。

normal.en: The two spellings differ only in the ending, and computing settles on program everywhere.
normal.cn: 两种拼写只差词尾，计算机领域各地都落在 program 上。

normal.en: The verb splits by object: you program a computer with code, and you program a timer with a setting.
normal.cn: 动词按宾语分工：给计算机编程是写代码，给定时器设程序是调设定。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill that keeps fluttering after the audience has gone, still deciding the order of a night that is over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张观众散场后仍在飘动的节目单，还在决定一个已经结束的夜晚的顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of paper sliding into a machine, and the machine growing a spine as it reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条滑进机器，机器一边读一边长出脊骨。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights blinking to a timetable nobody in the street can see.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的红绿灯按一张路人看不见的时间表眨眼。

examples.en: A well-written program can be read by another person without running it.
examples.cn: 写得好的程序，别人不运行也能读懂。

examples.en: The museum program lists four lectures and one concert.
examples.cn: 博物馆的活动日程列出四场讲座和一场音乐会。

examples.en: She programmed the irrigation system to water the field before dawn.
examples.cn: 她把灌溉系统设定在黎明前浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来个（gram）」——事先扑上去写下来的东西，就是计划与程序

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；计算机义始于二十世纪四十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one thread: something is written down in advance, first as a notice, then as an order of events, a printed list, a show, a set of machine instructions, a course, a funded scheme, and at last as the act of setting or coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线索展开：某事被事先写下来，先是通告，再是活动顺序、印刷节目单、播出节目、机器指令集、课程、拨款项目，最后是设定与编程这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of times and steps pinned to the wall, with a machine reading the sheet line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满时间与步骤的纸钉在墙上，机器一行行读着这张纸。

branches.en: PLAN AND SCHEME: an intention set down in advance, whether a household plan or a funded public scheme.
branches.cn: 计划与方案：事先写下的意图，无论家务安排还是拨款推行的公共项目。

branches.en: TIME ARRANGEMENT: an order of events in time, applied to people and then to devices that must act on cue.
branches.cn: 时间安排：按时间排出的活动顺序，先用于人，后用于必须按时动作的设备。

branches.en: LIST AND SHOW: the printed order becomes a booklet, and the booklet gives its name to the broadcast item.
branches.cn: 节目单与节目：印刷的顺序成为小册子，小册子又把名字让给播出的节目。

branches.en: CODE: the written sequence is now for a machine, first as a noun and then as the verb that puts it there.
branches.cn: 代码：写下的序列改为给机器用，先是名词，再是把序列装进去的动词。

branches.en: COURSE OF STUDY: a degree is also a sequence of steps completed in order, so schools use the same word.
branches.cn: 课程：学位同样是一串按顺序完成的步骤，学校于是沿用同一个词。

intro.en: Program is Greek in its two pieces, Latin in its noun ending and French in its modern shape. English then added -ing, -er and -able to build the computing family.
intro.cn: program 的两个构件来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，现代形式来自法语。英语随后加 -ing、-er、-able 构成计算机词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin programma is the one learned borrowing that carries the word from Greek into French and English; the other Latin-looking ending -atic came later through French adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 programma 是把这个词从希腊语带到法语与英语的唯一学术借词；另一个似拉丁的词尾 -atic 是后来经法语形容词进入的。

items.example: The prefix places the writing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「写」放在事情发生之前。

items.example: The verb names the act of setting marks down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把符号落下来的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the act of writing into a written thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「写」这个动作变成「写出来的东西」。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: a notice; an order of events
items.example: English took the French shape in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪接受了法语的形式。

items.meaning: a plan or a coded instruction set
items.example: The short spelling became standard in computing.
items.exampleCN: 短拼写在计算机领域成为标准。

items.example: Programming names the work rather than the product.
items.exampleCN: programming 指这项工作，而不是成品。

items.example: A programmer is the one who writes the code.
A programmable device can hold a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备能装入新的序列。

items.example: Programmatic music follows a written story.
items.exampleCN: 标题音乐遵循一个写好的故事。

definition_zh: 粉笔；白垩；用粉笔写（或画）
definition_en: soft white limestone used for writing; a stick of this material; to write with it
core_image: 一支白色粉笔在黑板上沙沙作响，留下白色痕迹
scene: 数学课前，值日生把三支白色粉笔放到讲台上。 The teacher wrote the date on the board with a piece of chalk.
sceneCN: 这里 chalk 是「粉笔」（第 1 个义项：能在黑板上写字的白条）；句意为老师用粉笔在黑板上写日期。

derivatives.zh: 由 chalk 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「白垩质的；发白的」
由 chalk 加 board 构成，义为「黑板」

senses.title: A stick for writing on a blackboard
senses.definition: a small stick of soft white material used for writing or drawing, especially on a blackboard
senses.definitionCN: 用软白材料做的小条，用来写字画画，尤指在黑板上
senses.example: He broke the chalk while writing quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他写得太快，把粉笔折断了。
senses.why: The writing stick is the everyday object named directly by the material it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 写字用的条状物直接以制材命名，因为它由这种白色软石做成。

senses.title: The soft white rock itself
senses.definition: a type of soft white limestone rock, formed from ancient sea creatures
senses.definitionCN: 一种白色软质石灰岩，由远古海洋生物形成
senses.example: The cliffs at Dover are made of white chalk.
senses.exampleCN: 多佛的悬崖由白色白垩构成。
senses.why: Before the stick, the rock itself carried the name; the stick is just the rock shaped for writing.
senses.whyCN: 先有岩石之名，后才有粉笔条；条不过是把这种岩石削成了写字的形状。

senses.title: To write or draw with chalk
senses.definition: to write or draw something using chalk
senses.definitionCN: 用粉笔写字或画画
senses.example: Someone chalked a smiley face on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在墙上用粉笔画了个笑脸。
senses.why: Materials often turn into verbs for using them, so the white stick also names the act of writing with it.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常转为使用它的动词，白条便也命名了用它书写的动作。

intro.en: Chalk goes back to a Latin word for lime or limestone, arriving in English through Germanic languages.
intro.cn: chalk 的源头是拉丁语中指「石灰」的词，经日耳曼诸语传入英语。

items.en: Latin calx meant limestone or lime, from a Greek word for pebble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calx 指石灰岩或石灰，源自一个指卵石的希腊词。

items.en: Old English cealc meant chalk or lime, borrowed from Latin via Germanic tribes.
items.cn: 古英语 cealc 指白垩或石灰，经日耳曼部落由拉丁语借入。

items.en: In Middle English, chalk named both the white rock and the writing stick.
items.cn: 中古英语里，chalk 既指白色岩层，也指写字的白条。

items.en: As schools spread, chalk became firmly linked to blackboard writing.
items.cn: 随着学校普及，chalk 与黑板书写牢固地联系起来。

items.en: Today chalk covers the writing stick, the white rock, and the verb of writing with it.
items.cn: 今天 chalk 涵盖粉笔条、白垩岩，以及用它书写的动词。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects related writing materials.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收相关书写材料类词。

entries.definition: The side of the face below the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脸颊」，读音与 chalk 相近。

entries.definition: To examine something to make sure it is right.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查」，拼写与 chalk 相近。

entries.definition: Whitish, like chalk.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「发白的」，由 chalk 派生。

entries.definition: A stick of coloured wax for drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜡笔」，同为书写画画的条状物。

entries.definition: A felt-tip pen for writing on boards.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记号笔」，在现代教室常代替粉笔。

entries.definition: A white substance from limestone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石灰」，与 chalk 同源于拉丁语 calx。

normalIntro.en: Remember chalk by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chalk。

normal.en: chalk comes from Latin calx, meaning limestone.
normal.cn: chalk 源自拉丁语 calx，意为石灰岩。

normal.en: chalkboard is the board you chalk on.
normal.cn: chalkboard 就是写粉笔字的黑板。

normal.en: chalky describes anything whitish like chalk.
normal.cn: chalky 形容一切像白垩的发白之物。

normal.en: the White Cliffs of Dover are famous chalk cliffs.
normal.cn: 多佛白崖是著名的白垩悬崖。

normal.en: chalk up means to score or record a success.
normal.cn: chalk up 意为记下、取得成绩。

abstract.en: Hear the soft squeak of white dust on the board.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见白灰在黑板上轻轻的吱吱声。

abstract.en: Picture a white cliff rising straight out of the sea.

intro.en: Gun has a surprisingly personal origin story involving a famous name.
intro.cn: gun 的起源出人意料地与一个人名有关。

items.en: The medieval female name Gunhild or Gunilda was shortened to Gun for engines of war.
items.cn: 中世纪女名 Gunhild（贡希尔）被缩略为 Gun，用来称呼战争器械。

items.en: Fourteenth-century English records name siege engines Gunilda, and the nickname spread to cannon.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语文献把攻城器械命名为 Gunilda，昵称随后传给火炮。

items.en: Some scholars connect the name to Old Norse gunnr meaning war, though this is debated.
items.cn: 有学者把该名字与古诺斯语 gunnr（战争）相连，但尚有争议。

items.en: By the fifteenth century gun meant any firearm, large or small.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，gun 已泛指各种火器，大小皆可。

items.en: Modern English added spray guns, nail guns, and the verb of accelerating.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了喷枪、射钉枪以及「猛加速」的动词义。

definition_en: happening, used or placed in the open air rather than inside a building
core_image: 学校后山草地上搭起的简易舞台，两旁的树当了幕布，观众就坐在草地上
scene: 春天一到，学校后山那片草地就成了舞台，孩子们把桌椅搬出去，在树荫下排节目。 The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.

senses.title: Happening in the open air
senses.definition: taking place outside a building rather than under a roof
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之外、而不是在屋顶之下举行
senses.example: The wedding was an outdoor ceremony in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是在花园里举行的户外仪式。
senses.why: The compound is out plus door, so whatever is outdoor happens beyond the doorway; the threshold is the line the word keeps pointing at.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是 out 加 door，所以户外的事情都发生在门之外；门槛就是这个词一直指着的那条线，义项直接落在「门外」的空间上。

senses.title: Open to the sky, without a roof
senses.definition: describing a place or structure that has no roof and is open to the weather
senses.definitionCN: 形容场所或构筑物没有屋顶，直接对着天气敞开
senses.example: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。
senses.why: A place beyond the door with nothing over it is exposed to sun and rain, so the word can describe the shelter as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 一个在门之外、头顶又空无一物的场所，就直接暴露在日晒雨淋之下，所以这个词既能说活动，也能说场所本身；露天义强调「没有遮蔽」这一层。

senses.title: Made for use outside
senses.definition: designed to be used in the open air, as clothes, furniture or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 专为在露天使用而设计，如衣物、家具或器材
senses.example: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。
senses.why: Once the word marks the open air, makers label whatever is built to endure that weather, and the adjective shifts from place to purpose.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出了露天场所，制造商就把为那种天气而造的东西也标上它，形容词便从「地点」转向「用途」；户外装备义由此而来。

intro.en: Outdoor is a compound of two Old English words, out and door, shortened from the older phrase out of doors in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: outdoor 是两个古英语词 out 与 door 的复合，十八世纪从较早的短语 out of doors 缩略而来。

items.en: The reconstructed forms ut and dur- gave both halves their Germanic shape, so the compound was built entirely inside English's own word family.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 与 dur- 给了两半各自的日耳曼形态，整个复合词都建在英语自身的词族之内。

items.en: Out came from the adverb ut, and door from duru, the word for an opening that can be shut.
items.cn: out 出自副词 ut，door 出自名词 duru，后者指可以关上的一个开口。

items.en: Middle English already said out of doors for being in the open air, a phrase that kept door as the boundary of the house.
items.cn: 中古英语已经用 out of doors 表示「在露天」，这个短语仍把门当作屋子的边界。

items.en: The three-word phrase was shortened into the single attributive adjective outdoor, which then stood before nouns like life and games.
items.cn: 这个三词短语缩成了一个作定语的形容词 outdoor，随后站到 life、games 这类名词前面。

items.en: Modern English keeps outdoor for the adjective, outdoors for the adverb, and pairs the word with indoor on the other side of the wall.
items.cn: 现代英语把 outdoor 留给形容词、outdoors 留给副词，并让这个词与墙另一侧的 indoor 成对使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the compound's own family and its mirror opposite; the near-meaning group gathers words for air, outside space and open dining.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词自己的词族与镜像反义词；近义组收表示露天、外部空间与户外用餐的词。

normal.en: Outdoors is the adverb and outdoor the adjective, and that final s is the only difference between them.
normal.cn: outdoors 是副词，outdoor 是形容词，两者的差别只在末尾那个 s。

normal.en: Indoor is the mirror image built the same way with in, so the pair marks the two sides of one wall.
normal.cn: indoor 是用 in 按同样办法造出的镜像，这一对词标出同一道墙的两侧。

normal.en: Outdoor furniture and outdoor clothes are named for the weather they must endure, not for the place alone.
normal.cn: outdoor furniture 与 outdoor clothes 是按它们必须承受的天气命名，而不只是按地点命名。

abstract.en: A stage set on grass with trees standing in for curtains is the word at its clearest.
abstract.cn: 草地上搭起的舞台、拿树当幕布，就是这个词最清楚的样子。

abstract.en: A doorway with sun on one side and shadow on the other is the line the word draws.
abstract.cn: 一道门，一侧有阳光、一侧有阴影，就是这个词划出的界线。

abstract.en: A pair of boots left by a tent shows the adjective following a person out of the house.
abstract.cn: 帐篷旁放着的一双靴子，显示这个形容词跟着人走出了屋子。

examples.en: The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.
examples.cn: 学校每年春天在草地上办一场户外音乐会。

examples.en: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。

examples.en: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
examples.cn: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特多」——奥在门外，多是门；门外的这片天，就是户外。

root: outdoor 由古英语 ut（在外）与 duru（门）合成，十八世纪从短语 out of doors 缩略为形容词；两半都属日耳曼语词族，没有拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a door; the senses move from an event held there, to a place with no roof, to the gear made to be used out there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是门的另一侧；义项从在那一侧举行的活动，转到没有屋顶的场所，再转到为在那一侧使用而造的装备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stage on a grassy slope behind the school, trees standing in for curtains, the audience seated on the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：学校后山坡草地上的简易舞台，树充当幕布，观众坐在草地上。

branches.en: a wedding standing on a garden lawn
branches.cn: 站在花园草坪上的婚礼

branches.en: a long table beside a river with no roof above
branches.cn: 河边上方无顶的长桌

branches.en: boots by a tent, made for wet ground
branches.cn: 帐篷旁为湿地而做的靴子

branches.en: one open space, used once for a ceremony and once for a meal
branches.cn: 同一片露天空地，一次用于仪式，一次用于吃饭

branches.en: clothing chosen for weather rather than for walls
branches.cn: 按天气而非按墙壁挑选的衣物

intro.en: The word joins an Old English adverb for outside with the Old English noun for door, then grows an adverb, an adjective and a mirror opposite from the same pattern.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在外」的副词与表示「门」的名词连在一起，再按同一模式长出副词、形容词与镜像反义词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；全部地
definition_en: totally and in every way; to the fullest degree
core_image: 一杯水被一口气喝光，一滴不剩
scene: 考试结束铃响了，小明忽然发现有一整页题没做，心一下子凉透了。 I had forgotten that page, so my answers were completely wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 completely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：程度达到顶点、一点不剩）；句意是我整页没做，答案全错了。

derivatives.zh: 由 complete 加副词后缀构成，义为「完整的；完成的」
义为「完成；使完整」
由 complete 加 -ion 构成，义为「完成；结束」

senses.title: To the greatest degree possible
senses.definition: totally, in every way, with nothing left out
senses.definitionCN: 在所有方面都如此，毫无保留
senses.example: The bottle was completely empty after the football match.
senses.exampleCN: 踢完足球赛后瓶子全空了。
senses.why: The core image is finishing something down to the last drop, so the adverb pushes the meaning all the way to the end.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把事情做到最后一滴也不剩，所以这个副词把程度推到顶点。

senses.title: In every part; wholly
senses.definition: in every part or detail; wholly so
senses.definitionCN: 在每个部分或细节上都如此
senses.example: My answer was completely different from hers.
senses.exampleCN: 我的答案和她的完全不同。
senses.why: When nothing is shared between two things, people say they differ completely, so the word also covers whole extent.
senses.whyCN: 当两个事物没有任何共同点时，人们说它们完全不同，所以这个词也表示范围上的全部。

senses.title: Used to emphasize a state or feeling
senses.definition: used before adjectives or verbs to make the meaning stronger
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词或动词前加强语气
senses.example: I completely forgot to bring my homework.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全忘了带作业。
senses.why: Because the word means without exception, it becomes a natural way to stress how total a feeling or mistake is.
senses.whyCN: 因为它表示毫无例外，所以成了强调感受或错误有多彻底的自然说法。

intro.en: Completely is built from Latin parts that mean to fill up.
intro.cn: completely 由拉丁语词根构成，本义是「填满」。

items.en: The Latin verb complere meant to fill up or finish, from com- (with) + plere (to fill).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 complere 意为填满、完成，由 com-（一起）+ plere（填）构成。

items.en: Old French turned complere into complir, meaning to carry out.
items.cn: 古法语把 complere 变成 complir，意为执行、实现。

items.en: English adopted complete in the fourteenth century as an adjective meaning finished.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 complete 作形容词，意为完成的。

items.en: The adverb completely appeared soon after, meaning wholly or totally.
items.cn: 副词 completely 随后出现，意为完全地、彻底地。

items.en: Today completely is one of the most common intensifiers in spoken English.
items.cn: 如今 completely 是英语口语中最常用的强调副词之一。

note.en: These words are all built on the complete family or express totality.
note.cn: 这些词都属于 complete 词族，或同样表达「全部」的概念。

entries.definition: finished; having all its parts
the act of finishing something
a nice thing you say to someone; note the i, different root
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；赞美（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: combining well to make a whole
entries.definitionCN: 互补的（与 complete 同源于 complere）

entries.definition: completely, in every way
wholly, with nothing missing
completely and without any doubt
completely; as a whole

normalIntro.en: Link completely to the complete family.
normalIntro.cn: 把 completely 和 complete 词族连起来记。

normal.en: complete = com- (with) + plere (to fill).
normal.cn: complete 由 com- 加 plere 构成，意为填满。

normal.en: completely = complete + -ly, turning an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: completely 由 complete 加 -ly 构成，形容词变副词。

normal.en: complete homework = finish every question.
normal.cn: complete 作动词指把作业每道题都做完。

normal.en: completely full means nothing more can go in.
normal.cn: completely full 指再也装不进任何东西。

normal.en: completely sounds like come-please; come in, please fill it completely.
normal.cn: completely 发音像 come-please，进来吧，请把它装满。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled to the very top rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一个杯子装到最顶端的边沿。

abstract.en: Picture wiping a blackboard so clean that no chalk marks remain.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板被擦得干干净净，一点粉笔印都没有。

abstract.en: Picture crossing out a whole page of wrong answers at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一次性划掉整页错误答案。

examples.en: The classroom was completely quiet during the test.
examples.cn: 考试期间教室里完全安静。

examples.en: I completely forgot about the basketball practice yesterday.
examples.cn: 我昨天完全忘了有篮球训练。

examples.en: Your new hairstyle makes you look completely different.
examples.cn: 你的新发型让你看起来完全不一样了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎普利特利」——露营（camp）时特别（利特）卖力（利）地干活，把营地彻底收拾干净，一点都不剩。

root: 拉丁语 complere（填满；完成），由 com-（一起）+ plere（填）构成。同族词有 completion（完成）、complementary（互补的）。

sensesIntro.en: From filled-up to all-the-way and emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「填满」引申到「全然」再到「强调」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: filled up with nothing left
core.cn: 核心意象：装满后一点不剩

branches.en: The degree is pushed to the maximum.
branches.cn: 程度被推到最大。

branches.en: Every part is covered.
branches.cn: 每个部分都被覆盖。

branches.en: The word stresses adjectives and verbs.
branches.cn: 这个词用来强调形容词和动词。

branches.en: Totality means nothing is left out.
branches.cn: 完全意味着毫无遗漏。

branches.en: The image of filling supports the stress use.
branches.cn: 填满的意象支撑了强调用法。

intro.en: Completely shows how a Latin verb became an everyday adverb.
intro.cn: completely 展示了拉丁语动词如何变成日常副词。

latinIntro.en: The root plere means to fill, and it fills many English words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 plere 意为填满，它填满了许多英语词。

items.example: The classmates cooperated, working with each other.
items.exampleCN: 同学们合作，彼此一起做事。

items.example: A full bucket has water filled to the top.
Please complete the form before the class.
A red scarf is the perfect complement to her coat.
items.exampleCN: 红围巾是她大衣的完美搭配。

items.meaning: to carry out; put into action
items.example: The school implemented a new reading plan.
items.exampleCN: 学校实施了一个新的阅读计划。

items.meaning: something added to fill a gap
items.example: She takes a vitamin supplement every day.
items.exampleCN: 她每天吃维生素补充剂。

items.example: We have plenty of time before the bus comes.
items.exampleCN: 公交车来之前我们有充足的时间。

definition_zh: 比赛；竞赛；竞争；对手
definition_en: an event in which people compete; the activity of competing
core_image: 赛场中央的奖杯，四面八方都是争它的手
scene: 教学楼前贴出了英语演讲比赛的海报。 The English speech competition opens next Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 competition 是「比赛」（第 1 个义项：有组织的竞赛活动）；句意是英语演讲比赛下周一开始。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「竞争；比赛」
由 compete 加 -or 构成，义为「选手；竞争者」
由 compete 加 -itive 构成，义为「竞争激烈的」

senses.title: An organized contest
senses.definition: an event where people try to win
senses.definitionCN: 人们争夺胜利的活动
senses.example: Our team entered the robot-building competition.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队参加了机器人搭建比赛。
senses.why: Rules and prizes turn trying into an event.
senses.whyCN: 规则与奖项让较量成为一场活动。

senses.title: The struggle against others
senses.definition: the effort to win business, marks or jobs
senses.definitionCN: 争取生意、分数或工作的较量
senses.example: Competition among classmates keeps scores rising.
senses.exampleCN: 同学间的竞争让分数不断上升。
senses.why: Same goal, many hands, not enough room for all.
senses.whyCN: 目标相同、人手众多，容不下所有人。

senses.title: The rivals as a whole
senses.definition: all the people or companies fighting for the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 争夺同一目标的所有人或公司
senses.example: Our shop's competition is the new mall nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 我们店的对手是附近的新商场。
senses.why: The rivals together get one name.
senses.whyCN: 对手合起来共用一个名字。

intro.en: Competition is compete dressed as a noun.
intro.cn: competition 是穿上名词外衣的 compete。

items.en: Latin competere meant to strive together for something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 competere 意为共同争取某物。

items.en: Competitio meant a coming together, later a contest.
items.cn: competitio 意为会合，后来指竞赛。

items.en: English took the word through Old French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪经古法语借入。

items.en: It first appeared in formal and legal writing.
items.cn: 它最初出现在正式与法律文书中。

items.en: Sport and markets made it an everyday word.
items.cn: 体育与市场使它成为日常用词。

note.en: Contest words and quiet opposites.
note.cn: 竞赛之词与安静的对照词。

entries.definition: a person in a competition
verb: to take part in a contest
adjective: keen to win
finishing something; letters close, different root
a competition
a sports game
ongoing competition between rivals
working together

normalIntro.en: Add -ition to compete and the contest appears.
normalIntro.cn: compete 加 -ition，比赛登场。

normal.en: competition = compete + -ition.
normal.cn: competition 由 compete 加 -ition 构成。

normal.en: a competition has rules, judges and prizes.
normal.cn: 比赛有规则、裁判和奖品。

normal.en: competition in business means fighting for customers.
normal.cn: 商业中的竞争指争夺顾客。

normal.en: the competition can mean all your rivals.
normal.cn: the competition 可指所有对手。

normal.en: win a competition and take the trophy.
normal.cn: 赢得比赛捧回奖杯。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard with two teams neck and neck.
abstract.cn: 想象比分板上两队不相上下。

abstract.en: Picture dozens of envelopes dropped into one prize box.
abstract.cn: 想象几十封信投进同一个抽奖箱。

abstract.en: Picture two lemonade stands side by side on one street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上并排的两个柠檬水摊。

examples.en: She practised every evening for the spelling competition.
examples.cn: 为了拼写比赛她每晚练习。

examples.en: The competition for the one scholarship was fierce.
examples.cn: 唯一一项奖学金的竞争非常激烈。

examples.en: Online stores brought new competition to our local market.
examples.cn: 网店给本地市场带来了新的竞争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯劈提身」——他肯下苦功劈开难题提升自身，就为上场比赛，所以「肯劈提身」= competition。

root: 拉丁语 com-（共同）+ petere（寻求）→ competitio（竞赛）→ 英语 competition。compete、competitor、appetite 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The contest event, the silent struggle and the rivals combined.
sensesIntro.cn: 竞赛活动、无声较量与对手全体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands reaching for one trophy
core.cn: 核心意象：众手同捧一奖杯

branches.en: School and city contests
branches.cn: 学校与市级比赛

branches.en: Grades, jobs and markets
branches.cn: 分数、职位与市场

branches.en: Rivals under one name
branches.cn: 合称的对手们

branches.en: Training hard to win
branches.cn: 为赢而苦练

branches.en: Business battles nearby
branches.cn: 身边的商业竞争

intro.en: One verb grows a whole contest family.
intro.cn: 一个动词长出整个竞赛词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin competitio already meant a contest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 competitio 已有竞赛之义。

items.example: Competition is the act of competing.

items.exampleCN: 这家店售价很有竞争力。

definition_zh: 请求；要求；请求的事物
definition_en: the act of politely asking for something, or the thing that is asked for
core_image: 一个人轻轻敲门，把写着自己需要的纸条递进去，等待对方点头
scene: 客人把需要更多毛巾的请求写在卡片上，前台很快送来了。 Her request for an extra towel was met within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 request 是「请求」（第 1 个义项：礼貌地开口要求某事）；句意：她要一条额外毛巾的请求几分钟内就得到了满足。

derivatives.zh: 请求者
被请求的；指定的

senses.title: The act of asking politely
senses.definition: the act of asking for something in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式方式提出要求的行为
senses.example: She made a request for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 她请求多给一些时间。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to seek again, so the core sense is the act of asking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「再次寻求」的动词，所以核心义是「开口要求」这个动作。

senses.title: The thing asked for
senses.definition: the thing that someone asks for
senses.definitionCN: 某人要求得到的东西
senses.example: His request was simple: a quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 他的请求很简单：一间安静的房间。
senses.why: The act of asking easily becomes the name of what is asked for.
senses.whyCN: 「请求」这个动作很容易转指「被请求的东西」。

senses.title: To ask formally
senses.definition: to ask for something in a polite or official way
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式的方式要求某事
senses.example: Guests are requested to keep their voices low.
senses.exampleCN: 请客人保持低声。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the noun's action into grammatical form, with the same polite or official tone.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词所指的动作变成语法形式，礼貌或正式的语气保持不变。

intro.en: Request comes through Old French requeste from Latin requirere, to seek again, from re- and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: request 经古法语 requeste 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），由 re- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire, and it also gives us question.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问，也是 question 的来源。

items.en: Requirere adds re- and means to seek again or ask for something needed.
items.cn: requirere 加上 re-，意为再次寻求或索取所需之物。

items.en: The noun requesta names a formal asking or petition.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语名词 requesta 指正式的请求或请愿。

items.en: Old French requeste carries the noun into English with a polite tone.
items.cn: 古法语 requeste 把这个名词带入英语，并带有礼貌语气。

items.en: Middle English request covers both the asking and the thing asked for.
items.cn: 中古英语 request 既指请求动作，也指所请求之物。

items.en: Modern English uses request as both noun and verb in formal settings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，request 在正式场合兼作名词和动词。

note.en: Request belongs to the seek-and-ask family, and it is close to words for appeals, applications, and demands.
note.cn: request 属于「寻求与询问」词族，与呼吁、申请和要求类词相邻。

entries.definition: to need or demand something
something that is needed or demanded
a person who makes a request
an urgent request for help or support
a formal written request signed by many people
a formal request for a job or place
a strong request that is hard to refuse

normalIntro.en: Request contains quest, the seeking root of question, so the memory picture is going out to seek something and asking politely for it.
normalIntro.cn: request 含有 quest 这个「寻求」词根，也见于 question，记忆画面是出去寻求并礼貌地开口。

normal.en: Re- means again, and quest means seek: seek again by asking.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，quest 表示寻求：通过开口再次寻求。

normal.en: Make a request is the standard phrase for the act.
normal.cn: make a request 是表示这个动作的标准搭配。

normal.en: On request means it will be given as soon as someone asks.
normal.cn: on request 意为「一经请求就提供」。

normal.en: At the request of marks who asked for it.
normal.cn: at the request of 标出是谁提出的请求。

normal.en: Compare require: to require is stronger and means need or demand.
normal.cn: 对比 require：语气更强，意为需要或要求。

abstract.en: Picture a note slipped under a hotel room door asking for towels.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条从酒店房门下塞进去，要求毛巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a raised hand in a quiet room waiting to be called on.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里举起一只手，等待被点到。

abstract.en: Think of a form filled out and handed across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象填好的表格被递过柜台。

examples.en: The manager granted her request for leave.
examples.cn: 经理批准了她的休假请求。

examples.en: All requests must be sent in writing.
examples.cn: 所有请求都必须以书面形式提交。

examples.en: Visitors are requested to sign in at the desk.
examples.cn: 请访客在前台登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ quest（寻求）＝再次开口寻求，即请求；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ quaerere（寻求、询问）→ requirere（再次寻求）→ 中世纪拉丁语 requesta → 古法语 requeste → 中古英语 request。

sensesIntro.en: The polite act of asking comes first, then the thing asked for, and the verb reuses the same shape for formal asking.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是礼貌开口的动作，再是被请求之物，动词则沿用同一形态表示正式请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polite note passed to someone who can grant what it asks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张礼貌的纸条递给有能力答应请求的人。

branches.en: The act of asking is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 开口请求的动作，是核心名词义项。

branches.en: The content of the asking becomes the thing requested.
branches.cn: 询问的内容成为「被请求之物」。

branches.en: The verb repeats the same act in a formal setting.
branches.cn: 动词在正式场合重复同一个动作。

branches.en: Act and object are two sides of one polite exchange.
branches.cn: 动作与对象是一次礼貌往来中的两面。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in grammar, not in the asking.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只在语法上不同，请求本身相同。

intro.en: Request is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin prefix and the seeking root quaerere.
intro.cn: request 是法语形态的名词，建立在拉丁前缀与「寻求」词根 quaerere 之上。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and quaerere means to seek or ask, so requirere is to seek again.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，quaerere 表示寻求或询问，所以 requirere 就是「再次寻求」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 request 与 require 开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of request and question.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 request 与 question 的词根。

items.example: Requirere supplies the stem of request.
items.exampleCN: requirere 提供 request 的词干。
requesta 在法语中变成 requeste。

definition_zh: 知识；学问；了解；知晓
definition_en: the information and understanding that a person has gained through learning or experience, or the state of being aware of something
core_image: 书架一排排立起，书脊连成一片灰色的墙
scene: 图书馆的顶层几乎无人，只有翻页的轻响。 Her knowledge of local history came mostly from old maps kept in the drawer.
sceneCN: 这里 knowledge 是「知识、学问」（第 1 个义项：通过学习积累的信息与理解），句意是她对本地历史的了解主要来自放在抽屉里的旧地图。画面里有安静的图书馆顶层与成排书脊。

pos.zh: 名词：知识；学问；了解；知晓（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 加 -able 构成，义为「博学的、有见识的」
由 know 加后缀构成，义为「故意地」
knowledge 的动词源头，义为「知道」
un- 与 knowledgeable 合成，义为「无知的、缺乏了解的」

senses.title: Information gained by learning
senses.definition: the facts, ideas, and skills that a person has learned over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个人长期学习积累的事实、观念与技能
senses.example: Her knowledge of chemistry is far beyond her years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的化学知识远超她的年龄。
senses.why: The noun gathers everything a person has learned into one store, the way a library holds books.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把一个人学到的一切汇成一座仓库，正如图书馆藏书。

senses.title: Understanding of a particular field
senses.definition: familiarity with a particular subject, gained by study or work
senses.definitionCN: 因学习或工作而对某一领域产生的熟悉
senses.example: He has a working knowledge of two programming languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他能实际使用两门编程语言。
senses.why: Knowledge is often counted by field, so people speak of a working knowledge of a subject.
senses.whyCN: 知识常按领域来计算，所以人们说对某学科有「够用的了解」。

senses.title: Being aware of a fact
senses.definition: the state of knowing about something, especially something private or official
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事的状态，尤指私事或正式事务
senses.example: The letter was sent without my knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信是在我不知情的情况下寄出的。
senses.why: This sense is not learning but awareness, the fact of being informed at a given moment.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项不是学问而是知情，指在某一刻被告知的事实。

senses.title: Common or shared information
senses.definition: the information that most people in a group or a society have
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体或社会里多数人掌握的信息
senses.example: It is common knowledge that the shop closes on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店星期一关门是众所周知的事。
senses.why: When the same facts spread through a group, the noun widens from one mind to a whole community.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的事实传遍一个群体，这个词就由一颗心扩展到整个共同体的范围。

intro.en: Knowledge was formed inside English from the verb know plus a suffix, so it has no Latin ancestry of its own.
intro.cn: knowledge 是英语内部由动词 know 加后缀构成的词，本身没有拉丁语血统。

items.en: The form knowlechen first meant to acknowledge, with the noun knowleching beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语形式 knowlechen 最初意为「承认」，旁边有名词 knowleching。

items.en: A shortened noun knowlege appears in the fourteenth century with the modern sense.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现缩短的名词 knowlege，已带现代的意义。

items.en: The root behind know is shared with German kennen, so the family is Germanic rather than Latin.
items.cn: know 的词根与德语 kennen 共享，所以这个词族属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: The suffix -ledge lost its force, so knowledge no longer looks like a derived word.
items.cn: 后缀 -ledge 失去了构词作用，knowledge 不再像派生词。

items.en: Phrases such as to my knowledge and common knowledge fix the awareness sense.
items.cn: to my knowledge 与 common knowledge 等说法固定了「知情」这一义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derived forms and neighbours of the word; the near-meaning group gathers other names for what is learned.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生形式与近邻词；近义组收其他指「所学之物」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective from this noun, meaning well informed.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词派生的形容词，义为「见多识广的」。

entries.definition: A verb from the same source, meaning to admit or to confirm receipt.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「承认、确认收到」。

entries.definition: A modern compound describing an industry built on information.
entries.definitionCN: 现代合成词，描述以信息为基础的产业。

entries.definition: Facts supplied or received, not yet organised into understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 被提供或获得的事实，尚未组织成理解。

entries.definition: The ability to judge well, grown from knowledge and experience.
entries.definitionCN: 由知识与经验长成的良好判断力。

entries.definition: Knowledge gained by formal study, especially in the humanities.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其在人文学科中通过正式学习获得的知识。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real English formation, the uncountable grammar and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的英语构词、不可数用法，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Knowledge is built from know plus a suffix that no longer works on its own.
normal.cn: knowledge 由 know 加一个如今已不能独立使用的后缀构成。

normal.en: It is uncountable: a piece of knowledge, not a knowledge.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 a piece of knowledge，不说 a knowledge。

normal.en: To my knowledge is the standard way of saying as far as I am informed.
normal.cn: to my knowledge 是「据我所知」的标准说法。

normal.en: Acknowledge is the same word family, with a prefix that means towards.
normal.cn: acknowledge 属同一词族，前缀表示「朝向」。

normal.en: Working knowledge means enough to use it, not enough to teach it.
normal.cn: working knowledge 指够用，而非足以教人。

abstract.en: Knowledge is a store rather than a possession: it grows when shared and shrinks when unused.
abstract.cn: 知识是仓库而不是财物：分享时变多，搁置时变少。

abstract.en: The word began as an act of admitting something, which is a reminder that knowing often starts with saying yes to a fact.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初指「承认」某事，这提醒我们：知道往往始于对一个事实说「是」。

abstract.en: To be without knowledge of a thing is not the same as to be ignorant of it; the first is simply not being told.
abstract.cn: 「不知情」与「无知」并不相同：前者只是没人告知。

examples.en: His knowledge of birds surprised the whole class.
examples.cn: 他对鸟类的知识让全班惊讶。

examples.en: To my knowledge, no one has applied for the post.
examples.cn: 据我所知，还没有人申请这个职位。

examples.en: The files were copied without her knowledge.
examples.cn: 这些文件是在她不知情的情况下被复制的。

dict_mnemonic.text: know 知道 + -ledge——知道的东西堆成一座库，就是知识

root: 中古英语 knowlechen「承认」之名 knowleching 缩短而来，由动词 know 加后缀 -ledge 构成，词根与德语 kennen 同源；十四世纪起表「知识、学问」，后又引申出「知晓、知情」义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the store of what has been learned, mastery of one field, the state of being informed, and facts shared by a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：所学之物的总和，对某一领域的掌握，知情状态，以及群体共有的常识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of books on shelves, everything learned standing in its place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排书立在架上，学到的一切各在其位。

branches.en: THE STORE LINE: everything learned is gathered into one noun.
branches.cn: 仓库线：学到的一切被收进一个名词。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: knowledge is often counted by subject or by job.
branches.cn: 领域线：知识常按学科或职业来计。

branches.en: THE AWARENESS LINE: to be in the knowledge is simply to have been told.
branches.cn: 知情线：处在 the knowledge 中，就是被告知过。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: common knowledge belongs to a whole group.
branches.cn: 共享线：common knowledge 属于整个群体。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the word was made inside English from know.
branches.cn: 形式线：这个词是在英语内部由 know 造出的。

intro.en: Knowledge is an English-made noun: a native verb plus a suffix that has lost its independent meaning.
intro.cn: knowledge 是英语自造的名词：本族动词加一个已失去独立意义的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is Germanic, but the Latin words below belong to the same ancient knowing root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身是日耳曼语，但下面这些拉丁词属于同一古老的「知」词根。

items.meaningCN: 构成抽象名词，现已固化
items.exampleCN: 它把 know 变成 knowledge。

items.example: It forms the older form knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较早的形式 knowledge。

definition_zh: 人群；一群人；挤满；拥挤
definition_en: a large group of people close together; to fill a space with too many people or things
core_image: 体育场门口涌动的人潮
scene: 校运会开幕式上，操场四周站满了挥舞小旗的同学。 A big crowd gathered to watch the relay race.
sceneCN: 这里 crowd 是「人群」（第 1 个义项：密集聚在一起的一群人）；句意是一大群人聚在一起观看接力赛。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「拥挤的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「拥挤；聚集」
由 crowded 加 -ness 构成，义为「拥挤程度」

senses.title: A large group of people together
senses.definition: many people gathered close together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 许多人密集地聚在同一地方
senses.example: The crowd cheered when the runners crossed the line.
senses.exampleCN: 选手冲线时人群欢呼起来。
senses.why: The core image is many bodies pressed into one space, so any dense group is a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是许多身体挤在同一空间，所以任何密集的人群都是 crowd。

senses.title: To fill a space with too much
senses.definition: to fill a place completely, often too completely
senses.definitionCN: 把一个地方完全填满，常常太满
senses.example: Too many desks crowd the small classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 太多课桌把小教室挤得满满的。
senses.why: When the group presses into a room, the room itself is said to be crowded by them.
senses.whyCN: 当人群挤进房间时，就说房间被他们挤满了。

senses.title: To press close around someone
senses.definition: to gather closely around a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧围在某人或某物周围
senses.example: Fans crowded around the singer for photos.
senses.exampleCN: 歌迷们围住歌手拍照。
senses.why: The mass moves as one toward its centre of attention, so surrounding someone is crowding.
senses.whyCN: 人群朝焦点整体移动，所以围住某人就是 crowding。

intro.en: Crowd first named a pressing instrument, then the pressing itself.
intro.cn: crowd 最初指一种挤压器具，后来才指挤压本身。

items.en: The Old English crudan meant to press or thrust, like a fiddle bow.
items.cn: 古英语 crudan 意为推挤，也与提琴弓相关。

items.en: It came from a Germanic root about pushing, shared with Dutch kruden.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼语中表示推挤的词根，与荷兰语 kruden 同源。

items.en: The verb crowden meant to press forward in a mass.
items.cn: 中古英语动词 crowden 意为成群向前挤。

items.en: The noun crowd then named the mass of people doing the pressing.
items.cn: 名词 crowd 随之指正在挤压的人群。

items.en: Today crowd names groups, full buses and fan circles alike.
items.cn: 如今 crowd 指人群、满员的公交车和歌迷圈。

note.en: These words share the crowd family or name groups of people.
note.cn: 这些词属于 crowd 词族，或指人群。

the act of pressing together
a royal head cover; spelled a bit alike, different root
entries.definitionCN: 王冠（拼写略近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to bend low; sounds similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 蹲下（读音相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The pressing root and daily places hold crowd in place.
normalIntro.cn: 「推挤」词根与日常场所让 crowd 落位。

normal.en: crowd = press: many bodies pushing into one space.
normal.cn: crowd ＝推挤：许多身体挤进一个空间。

normal.en: crowd + ed = crowded, full of people.
normal.cn: crowd + ed ＝ crowded，人满为患的。

normal.en: A crowd of fans is smaller than a crowd of strangers.
normal.cn: a crowd of fans 比 a crowd of strangers 更有序。

normal.en: crowd around: form a ring around the star.
normal.cn: crowd around：围着明星围成一圈。

normal.en: The bus is crowded at seven every morning.
normal.cn: 公交车每天早上七点都很挤。

abstract.en: Hear the wave of cheers roll from the stands at the sports meet.
abstract.cn: 听运动会看台上欢呼的声浪滚过。

abstract.en: Feel the squeeze of the school bus at gate time.
abstract.cn: 感受校门口上车时的挤压。

abstract.en: See red scarves bob in one sea of heads at the flag-raising.
abstract.cn: 看升旗时一片红领巾在人海中起伏。

examples.en: The crowd waved little flags at the opening ceremony.
examples.cn: 人群在开幕式上挥舞着小旗。

examples.en: Don't crowd the door; let people out first.
examples.cn: 别挤在门口，先让人出去。

examples.en: The street was crowded with shoppers before Spring Festival.
examples.cn: 春节前街上挤满了购物的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠绕得」——人群挤来挤去，只能「靠」「绕」着「得」过去

root: 来自古英语 crudan（推挤），属日耳曼语词根；本义「挤」，后名词化为「挤压的人群」，动词与名词在「挤压」这一意象上相通。

sensesIntro.en: From pressing bodies, to full rooms, to rings around a star.
sensesIntro.cn: 从推挤的身体，到爆满的房间，再到围绕明星的人圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many bodies pressed into one space
core.cn: 核心意象：许多身体挤进同一空间

branches.en: Fans and runners at a sports meet
branches.cn: 运动会上的观众与选手

branches.en: Buses and rooms too full
branches.cn: 太满的公交车与房间

branches.en: Rings around a singing star
branches.cn: 围着歌星的人圈

branches.en: The mass moves toward its centre
branches.cn: 人群向中心移动

branches.en: Pressure makes the room crowded
branches.cn: 挤压使房间拥挤

intro.en: Crowd is a plain Germanic root with simple endings.
intro.cn: crowd 是朴素的日耳曼词根，词尾也简单。

latinIntro.en: Crowd is Germanic, not Latin, so latinEntries stay empty.
latinIntro.cn: crowd 是日耳曼词，不是拉丁词，latinEntries 为空。

definition_zh: 牙医；牙科医生
definition_en: a doctor who takes care of people's teeth
core_image: 举着小镜子和探针查看牙齿的白衣人
scene: 校医说我有一颗牙要检查。 The dentist showed me how to brush the teeth at the back properly.
sceneCN: 这里 dentist 是「牙医」（第 1 个义项：护理牙齿的医生）；句意是牙医教我正确刷后面的大牙。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根 dent（牙）加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「牙齿的」
由 dentist 加名词后缀 -ry 构成，义为「牙科学」
由 tri-（三）加 dent 构成，义为「三叉戟」

senses.title: A doctor for teeth
senses.definition: a person trained to look after and treat teeth
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、检查和治疗牙齿的人
senses.example: The dentist says I should floss every night.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医说我应该每晚用牙线。
senses.why: Latin dens means tooth, and -ist names the person of a trade, so the tooth person is a dentist.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dens 意为「牙」，后缀 -ist 表示从业者，掌管牙齿的人便是牙医。

senses.title: The clinic or practice place
senses.definition: the place or business where a dentist works, used informally
senses.definitionCN: 牙医工作的地方，口语中代指诊所
senses.example: Mum is at the dentist this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈今天下午在牙科诊所。
senses.why: People often name the worker to mean the workplace, like saying school for a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 人们习惯用从业者的名字代指其工作场所，就像用 school 代指上课一样。

intro.en: Dentist comes from Latin dens, a tooth.
intro.cn: dentist 来自拉丁语 dens（牙齿）。

items.en: Dens meant tooth; the related form dentis gave the stem dent-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dens 意为牙，相关形式 dentis 给出词干 dent-。

items.en: French formed dentiste from dent plus the trade ending -iste.
items.cn: 法语由 dent 加职业后缀 -iste 构成 dentiste。

items.en: Before dentist, English used the phrase tooth-drawer for such workers.
items.cn: 在 dentist 出现前，英语用 tooth-drawer（拔牙人）称呼这类从业者。

items.en: The word dentist was borrowed in the eighteenth century as a learned form.
items.cn: dentist 一词于十八世纪作为学术化借词进入英语。

items.en: Dentistry, dental and denture grew from the same stem.
items.cn: dentistry、dental、denture 都由同一词干派生。

note.en: These words share the Latin tooth root or name medical workers.
note.cn: 这些词与拉丁「牙」词根同源，或同样称呼医务工作者。

a doctor who operates

normalIntro.en: Use the tooth root and the -ist ending to remember dentist.
normalIntro.cn: 用「牙」词根和 -ist 后缀记住 dentist。

normal.en: dent- means tooth in Latin.
normal.cn: 词根 dent- 在拉丁语中表示牙齿。

normal.en: dental means about teeth.
normal.cn: dental 表示与牙齿有关的。

normal.en: -ist names a worker: artist, dentist, scientist.
normal.cn: -ist 表从业者：artist、dentist、scientist。

normal.en: trident has three teeth on its blade.
normal.cn: trident 的刃上有三个齿（三叉戟）。

normal.en: dentistry is the whole trade.
normal.cn: dentistry 指整个牙科行业。

abstract.en: Picture a small mirror peeking at each tooth.
abstract.cn: 想象一面小镜子逐颗查看牙齿。

abstract.en: Hear the gentle tick of the mirror on enamel.
abstract.cn: 听小镜子轻敲牙釉质的轻响。

abstract.en: Feel the proud smile after a clean check-up.
abstract.cn: 体会检查通过后骄傲的微笑。

examples.en: I was a little nervous before seeing the dentist, but it did not hurt.
examples.cn: 看牙医前我有点紧张，但其实并不疼。

examples.en: The dentist gave me a sticker after fixing my tooth.
examples.cn: 牙医补完牙后给了我一张贴纸。

examples.en: Our class learned dental care from a visiting dentist.
examples.cn: 我们班听来访的牙医讲了牙齿护理知识。

core.cn: 核心意象：守护每颗牙的细心的人

intro.en: Dentist joins the Latin tooth root with a trade ending.
intro.cn: dentist 由拉丁「牙」词根加职业后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root dent- means tooth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 dent- 意为牙齿。

definition_zh: 确定的；肯定的；必然的；某个；某些
definition_en: sure to happen or be true; fixed and not doubted; a particular thing not named
core_image: 把一块石头放在地上，它绝不会再移动
scene: 考试前我复习了三遍，答案早已记牢。 I felt certain about every answer on the test.
sceneCN: 这里 certain 是「确定的」（第 1 个义项：毫不怀疑）；句意是考试前我复习三遍，对每个答案都很有把握。

derivatives.zh: 由 certain 加 -ly 构成，义为「当然；确定地」
由 certain 加 -ty 构成，义为「确定；必然的事」
由 un- 加 certain 构成，义为「不确定的」

senses.title: Sure; without doubt
senses.definition: completely sure that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 完全确信某事属实或将会发生
senses.example: I am certain that I locked the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我确信自己锁了门。
senses.why: Something fixed in place cannot move, just as a fact you cannot doubt.
senses.whyCN: 固定不动的石头就像无法怀疑的事实。

senses.title: Sure to happen
senses.definition: certain to happen and impossible to stop or change
senses.definitionCN: 一定会发生、无法阻止或改变的
senses.example: Rain is certain this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午肯定会下雨。
senses.why: If there is no doubt at all, the result must follow.
senses.whyCN: 若毫无悬念，结果必然到来。

senses.title: A particular one not named
senses.definition: a particular thing or person that you do not name exactly
senses.definitionCN: 某个未具体说明的人或事物
senses.example: A certain student keeps forgetting homework.
senses.exampleCN: 有个学生总是忘带作业。
senses.why: When you know something but keep it vague, the word points without naming.
senses.whyCN: 当你心里有数却不愿点明时，这个词指而不名。

intro.en: Certain means held fast, so doubt cannot shake it.
intro.cn: certain 本义是「被牢牢固定」，怀疑无法撼动。

items.en: Latin certus means fixed, settled, decided.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为「固定的、已决定的」。

items.en: It grew from the verb cernere, to sift and decide.
items.cn: 它由动词 cernere（筛分、判定）发展而来。

items.en: Old French turned it into certain, meaning settled or sure.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 certain，意为「已定、确定」。

items.en: English adopted the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪吸收了该词。

items.en: Later it added the use for an unnamed particular thing.
items.cn: 后来它又增加了指「某个未点明事物」的用法。

note.en: Words about sureness and its shadow, doubt.
note.cn: 关于「确定」及其阴影「怀疑」的词。

entries.definition: adverb form: surely, of course
the state of being sure
not sure; doubtful
a cloth hung over a window; sounds close but is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 窗帘（发音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: certain; confident
feeling sure about yourself or a result
not certain; full of doubt
clear and fixed

normalIntro.en: Hold the word with cert- and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住词根 cert- 和它的家族。

normal.en: cert- means fixed and sure.
normal.cn: 词根 cert- 表示固定、确定。

normal.en: certain = cert + -ain, fixed and settled.
normal.cn: certain 由 cert 加 -ain 构成，确定的。

normal.en: certainly = certain + -ly, surely.
normal.cn: certainly 由 certain 加 -ly 构成，当然。

normal.en: uncertain = un- + certain, not sure.
normal.cn: uncertain 由 un- 加 certain 构成，不确定。

normal.en: for certain means with no doubt left.
normal.cn: for certain 意为毫无疑问。

abstract.en: Picture a rock glued to the ground that nothing can move.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被粘在地上的岩石，谁都搬不动。

abstract.en: Picture a student raising a hand with a bright, sure smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一个学生带着自信的微笑举手。

abstract.en: Picture rain clouds rolling in while you hold an umbrella ready.
abstract.cn: 想象乌云滚滚而来，你早已备好伞。

examples.en: It is certain that our team will reach the final.
examples.cn: 我们队一定会进入决赛。

examples.en: I am certain I put my keys on this desk.
examples.cn: 我确信把钥匙放在这张桌子上了。

examples.en: A certain boy in my class draws wonderful cartoons.
examples.cn: 我们班有个男孩画的卡通特别棒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟腾」——他板着脸稳稳「坐」在椅子上纹丝不动，像被钉住一样，十分确定，所以「瑟腾」= certain。

root: 拉丁语 cernere（筛分、判定）→ certus（确定的）→ 古法语 certain → 英语 certain。certify、certificate、certainty 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From a settled fact to a settled future and a hidden name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从确定的事实到必然的未来，再到未点明的某者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fixed so firmly that doubt cannot move it
core.cn: 核心意象：固定得怀疑无法撼动

branches.en: A fact you trust
branches.cn: 你信任的事实

branches.en: A future that must come
branches.cn: 必然会来的未来

branches.en: A name kept hidden
branches.cn: 被隐藏的名字

branches.en: Confidence in plans
branches.cn: 对计划的信心

branches.en: Answering with full belief
branches.cn: 满怀信念地回答

intro.en: Cert- is the root of being sure.
intro.cn: cert- 是「确定」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin certus, fixed, supplies the stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 certus（固定的）提供词干。

items.example: A certain fact cannot be shaken.

items.meaning: a French ending used in adjectives
items.example: Certain keeps the Old French ending.
I will certainly come to your party.
items.exampleCN: 我一定会来参加你的聚会。

items.example: Death and taxes are a certainty.
items.exampleCN: 死亡和纳税是必然的事。

items.example: The weather is uncertain these days.

items.meaning: to state that something is true
items.example: The doctor certified that he was fit.
She won a certificate in the contest.

definition_zh: 囚犯；俘虏；被扣押者；受困于……的人
definition_en: a person kept in prison as a punishment; a person captured in war or held captive; a person held by a group; and anyone trapped by a situation they cannot leave
core_image: 铁栏后面抬起的一张脸，眼睛还盯着门外的一点光
scene: 探视室的玻璃上蒙着一层雾，穿灰色衣服的人把手掌贴在另一侧，隔着反光的表面与家人对视。 The prisoner pressed one hand to the glass and tried to smile.
sceneCN: 这里 prisoner 指「囚犯」（第 1 个义项：在狱中服刑的人）；句意为那名囚犯把一只手贴在玻璃上，努力笑了一下。图中可辨识物件：探视玻璃、灰色衣服、贴在玻璃上的手掌。

pos.zh: 囚犯；俘虏；被扣押者；受困于……的人

derivatives.zh: 由 prison 加前缀 im- 构成，义为「监禁」，与 prisoner 同族
由 imprison 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「监禁；关押」
prisoner 的词干，义为「监狱；监禁」，加表人后缀后指被关在里面的人

senses.title: A person kept in a prison as punishment
senses.definition: a person who is kept in a prison while serving a sentence for a crime
senses.definitionCN: 因犯罪在狱中服刑、被关押的人
senses.example: The prisoner was allowed one hour of exercise a day.
senses.exampleCN: 那名囚犯每天获准活动一小时。
senses.why: The Old French ending -ier marked a person connected with something, so prisonier was simply the person who belonged to a prison.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词尾 -ier 标记「与某事物相关的人」，所以 prisonier 就是属于监狱的那个人。

senses.title: A person captured by an enemy in war
senses.definition: a soldier or civilian taken by an enemy force and held during a war
senses.definitionCN: 战争中被敌方捉住并扣押的军人或平民
senses.example: The soldiers were taken prisoner before they reached the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们还没到河边就被俘虏了。
senses.why: War produced captives long before modern prisons existed, and the same word covered them because both were people held against their will.
senses.whyCN: 早在现代监狱出现之前，战争就已经产生俘虏；同一个词能兼指两者，因为他们都是被违背意愿扣住的人。

senses.title: A person held captive by a group, often for bargaining
senses.definition: a person seized and held by a group, sometimes to force others to meet demands
senses.definitionCN: 被某一群体捉住扣留的人，有时用来迫使他人答应条件
senses.example: The prisoner was released after two weeks of negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两周谈判，那名被扣押者获释了。
senses.why: Once the word means anyone held, it fits a hostage as well; what differs is who holds the power, not the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词泛指任何被扣住的人，它自然也能指人质；不同的只是谁握着权力，而不是词本身。

senses.title: A person trapped by a situation or habit
senses.definition: a person who cannot escape a condition, relationship or habit that limits them
senses.definitionCN: 无法摆脱某种限制自己的处境、关系或习惯的人
senses.example: He became a prisoner of his own routine and stopped travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了自己日常习惯的囚徒，不再出门旅行。
senses.why: The literal cell becomes a metaphor: whatever a person cannot walk away from can be named as the thing that holds them prisoner.
senses.whyCN: 真实的牢房转成比喻：凡是人走不开的东西，都可以被说成把他困住的那个东西。

intro.en: Prisoner is the person-shaped member of the prison family: French put its ending for an involved person onto prison, and English borrowed the whole word rather than building it fresh.
intro.cn: prisoner 是 prison 词族里「人」的那一个：法语把表示「相关之人」的词尾加到 prison 上，英语整词借入，而不是自己新造。

items.en: Prehendere meant to seize, and its noun prehensio named the taking of a person into custody.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住，其名词 prehensio 指把人拿获、看管。

items.en: Old French prison named both captivity and the place where captives were kept.
items.cn: 古法语 prison 既指被囚禁，也指关押被囚者的地方。

items.en: Adding the ending -ier, which marked a person concerned with something, produced prisonier, the person held.
items.cn: 加上表示「与某事相关的人」的词尾 -ier，得到 prisonier，即被关押的那个人。

items.en: English borrowed the form as prisoner and used it for captives in war as well as for people in gaols.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 prisoner，既指狱中的人，也指战场上的俘虏。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word for legal inmates and extends it to hostages and to anyone trapped by circumstances.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它指法律意义上的在押者，并扩展到人质以及任何被处境困住的人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the prison stem and its Latin source; the near-meaning group gathers the other English names for people who are held.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 prison 词干及其拉丁语来源展开；近义组收英语里其他指「被扣住的人」的名称。

entries.definition: The place or state that gives prisoner its stem.
entries.definitionCN: 给出 prisoner 词干的地点或状态。

entries.definition: To put someone into prison; formed with the prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人关进监狱；由前缀 im- 构成。

entries.definition: The act or state of being imprisoned.
Able to grasp; from the same Latin root for seizing that stands behind prison.
entries.definitionCN: 能够抓握的；出自 prison 背后那个表示抓取的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: A person held by an enemy or a captor.
entries.definitionCN: 被敌人或捕获者扣住的人。

entries.definition: A person living in a prison or another institution.
entries.definitionCN: 住在监狱或其他机构里的人。

entries.definition: A person found guilty of a crime and serving a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 被判定有罪并在服刑的人。

entries.definition: A person kept in official custody, often without a criminal sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方羁押的人，常常并未被判刑。

normalIntro.en: This is a place word with a person ending on it, so the useful reminders keep the stem and the ending separate and then let them travel into war and metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 这是一个地点词加表人词尾构成的词，所以有用的记忆法是先把词干和词尾分开，再看它怎样走进战场和比喻。

normal.en: Prisoner is prison plus the old French ending -ier, which names a person connected with a place or thing.
normal.cn: prisoner 是 prison 加古法语词尾 -ier，那个词尾命名与某地或某物相关的人。

normal.en: The same ending appears in officer and grenadier, all of them people attached to something.
normal.cn: 同一个词尾也出现在 officer 和 grenadier 里，它们都指依附于某物的人。

normal.en: Prison supplies the stem: take away the ending and you have the place.
normal.cn: prison 提供词干：去掉词尾，剩下的就是那个地方。

normal.en: Take prisoner is a fixed phrase in which the verb means to capture, not to jail.
normal.cn: take prisoner 是固定说法，其中的动词是「俘获」，不是「关进监狱」。

normal.en: Prisoner of war keeps the old sense of a captive taken in battle, which predates the modern prison.
normal.cn: prisoner of war 保留了战场上被俘的旧义，那一层比现代监狱更早。

abstract.en: One word holds the man behind bars and the man on a battlefield, because both have lost the power to walk away.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着铁栏后的人和战场上的人，因为两者都失去了走开的权力。

abstract.en: The ending is what makes it personal: the place stays a place until -ier turns it into someone.
abstract.cn: 词尾让它变成了人：地点本来只是地点，直到 -ier 把它变成某个人。

abstract.en: A prisoner of habit shows how easily a legal word becomes a picture of the mind.
abstract.cn: 「习惯的囚徒」说明一个法律词多么容易变成一幅心理画面。

examples.en: The prisoner pressed one hand to the glass and tried to smile.
examples.cn: 那名囚犯把一只手贴在玻璃上，努力笑了一下。

examples.en: The soldiers were taken prisoner before they reached the river.
examples.cn: 士兵们还没到河边就被俘虏了。

examples.en: He became a prisoner of his own routine and stopped travelling.
examples.cn: 他成了自己日常习惯的囚徒，不再出门旅行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里兹纳」——被关在里面的人，只能数着窗格上的影子。

root: prison（监狱）加表人后缀 -er（来自古法语 -ier，源自拉丁语 -arius）；prison 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 prehensio（拿获）、prehendere（抓住）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person held by force; the senses divide by who holds them: the court, the enemy, an armed group, and finally a condition of the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个被强力扣住的人」；义项按扣押者分开：法庭、敌人、武装团伙，最后是心里的某种处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lifted behind iron bars, eyes fixed on a patch of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁栏后抬起的一张脸，眼睛盯着外面的一点光。

branches.en: a hand flat against visiting-room glass
branches.cn: 贴在探视室玻璃上的手掌

branches.en: a column of captured men on a road
branches.cn: 路上被押走的一队人

branches.en: a locked room and a negotiator outside
branches.cn: 锁着的房间与门外的谈判者

branches.en: a man who never leaves his own street
branches.cn: 从不走出自己那条街的人

branches.en: the same word for the jailed and the captured
branches.cn: 被关的与被俘的共用同一个词

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of seizing, its noun of arrest, the French place word, the French person ending, and the English noun that grew from them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示抓取的拉丁语动词、表示逮捕的名词、法语的地点词、法语的表人词尾，以及由它们长出的英语名词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb of seizing and its noun of arrest are recorded, and the French person ending -ier is itself a descendant of Latin -arius, so the whole word is Latin in its bones.
latinIntro.cn: 表示抓取的拉丁语动词与表示逮捕的名词都有记录，法语的表人词尾 -ier 本身也是拉丁语 -arius 的后代，所以这个词骨子里是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 建议；忠告；意见；咨询
definition_en: an opinion or a suggestion offered to help someone decide
core_image: 朋友在桌边给你出主意
scene: 放学后，朋友坐在桌边帮我分析该选哪门兴趣课。 She gave me good advice about the choice.
sceneCN: 这里 advice 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：帮助别人作决定的意见）；句意为她就这个选择给了我很好的建议。

pos.zh: 名词：建议；忠告；意见；咨询

derivatives.zh: 建议；劝告
顾问
顾问的；咨询的

senses.title: A suggestion about what to do
senses.definition: an opinion offered about what someone should do
senses.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做给出的看法
senses.example: She gave me some good advice.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了我一些好建议。
senses.why: Advice comes from Old French avis, a view or an opinion, so giving advice is giving someone a view to follow.
senses.whyCN: advice 来自古法语 avis「看法」，把看法给别人，就是建议。

senses.title: A serious warning
senses.definition: a careful word about what is wise or unwise
senses.definitionCN: 关于什么明智、什么不明智的郑重提醒
senses.example: He took his father's advice.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了父亲的忠告。
senses.why: When the view carries care about a risk, it becomes a serious warning.
senses.whyCN: 当这个看法带着对风险的关心，就成了郑重的忠告。

senses.title: An expert opinion
senses.definition: the opinion of someone who knows a field well
senses.definitionCN: 懂行的人给出的看法
senses.example: Ask a doctor for advice.
senses.exampleCN: 去问医生的专业意见。
senses.why: The same word covers the view of an expert, which is advice in a professional matter.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖专家的看法，那就是专业意见。

intro.en: The recorded history of advice is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 advice 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Visum meant something seen, from the verb to see.
items.cn: visum 意为看到的东西，来自表示看的动词。

items.en: Avis meant an opinion, a view that one holds.
items.cn: avis 意为意见，即一个人所持的看法。

items.en: English borrowed advice for an opinion offered to another.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪借入 advice，指提供给别人的意见。

items.en: The noun advice and the verb advise later took different spellings.
items.cn: 名词 advice 与动词 advise 后来采用了不同拼写。

items.en: Today it covers everything from a friend's tip to a lawyer's opinion.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖从朋友的提示到律师的意见。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give advice.
A person who gives advice.
An adjective meaning giving advice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为提供咨询的。

entries.definition: It stresses an idea put forward.
It stresses what someone thinks is true.
entries.definitionCN: 强调某人认为正确的东西。

entries.definition: A short, practical piece of advice.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: avis meant opinion, from a root meaning to see: advice is a view offered to someone.
normal.cn: avis 意为意见，词根意为看：advice 就是提供给别人看的看法。

normal.en: The same family also gives advise and adviser.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 advise 与 adviser。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase good advice.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「好建议」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of advice in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 advice 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: an opinion or a suggestion offered to help someone decide.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「建议」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a friend sitting at a table and giving you ideas.
abstract.cn: 想象朋友在桌边给你出主意。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She gave me some good advice.
examples.cn: 她给了我一些好建议。

examples.en: He took his father's advice.
examples.cn: 他接受了父亲的忠告。

examples.en: Ask a doctor for advice.
examples.cn: 去问医生的专业意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德维斯」——朋友在桌边给你出主意：建议

root: advice 来自古法语 avis「意见」，源头是拉丁语 visum「看到的东西」，来自表示看的动词；英语十三世纪借入，指提供给别人的意见，名词 advice 与动词 advise 后来采用了不同拼写，今天它涵盖从朋友提示到律师意见的各种建议。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of advice grows from one core image: a friend sitting at a table and giving you ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: advice 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：朋友在桌边给你出主意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a friend sitting at a table and giving you ideas
core.cn: 核心意象：朋友在桌边给你出主意

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：建议。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: A serious warning.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：忠告。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: An expert opinion.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：专业意见。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：建议、忠告。

branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：建议、专业意见。

intro.cn: advice 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

definition_zh: 环境；自然环境；周围状况；氛围
definition_en: the conditions, objects, and forces that surround a person, animal, or thing
core_image: 围在人身外的一圈：空气、水、人、规则都在圈里
scene: 森林样方里，研究员记录着温湿度等圈内的全部条件。 The biologist recorded the temperature and humidity of the forest environment.
sceneCN: 这里 environment 是「（生物所处的）环境条件」（第 3 个义项：生物生活的周围条件）；句意：生物学家记录了森林环境的温度和湿度。图中可辨识物件：温湿度计、森林、记录本、树冠与苔藓。
