senses.title: The act of surrounding: what lies around
senses.definition: the conditions, objects, or forces that surround a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 环绕着人、动物或事物的条件、物体或力量
senses.example: The laboratory environment must be kept free of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室环境必须保持无尘。
senses.why: Environ came from Old French environer 'to surround', built on viron 'a circle'. Environment first named the state of being encircled, then the things doing the encircling.
senses.whyCN: environ 来自古法语 environer“环绕”，建立在 viron“圆圈”上。environment 最初指“被围住的状态”，随后指做包围的那些东西。

senses.title: The natural world: air, water, land, and life
senses.titleCN: 自然世界：空气、水、土地与生命
senses.definition: the natural world, especially as affected by human activity
senses.definitionCN: 自然世界，尤指受到人类活动影响时
senses.example: Plastic waste is one of the biggest threats to the environment.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料垃圾是对环境的最大威胁之一。
senses.why: From the 1950s ecology gave the surrounding circle a planetary meaning: the whole natural system that surrounds and supports life.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪 50 年代起，生态学给了这个包围圈一层行星级含义：围绕并支撑生命的整个自然系统。

senses.title: Living conditions: where an organism lives
senses.titleCN: 生存条件：生物生活的地方
senses.definition: the conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates
senses.definitionCN: 人、动物或植物生活或运作所处的条件
senses.example: Cacti grow well in a dry environment.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌在干燥环境中长得好。
senses.why: For a living thing, the circle that surrounds it is made of climate, food, and shelter; the general surround narrows to a habitat.
senses.whyCN: 对生物来说，围住它的那个圈由气候、食物和庇护所构成；泛泛的“周围”缩小成了栖息环境。

senses.title: Social and cultural surroundings
senses.definition: the social, cultural, or economic conditions that shape behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 塑造行为的社会、文化或经济条件
senses.example: Children raised in a bilingual environment switch languages easily.
senses.exampleCN: 在双语环境中长大的孩子切换语言很轻松。
senses.why: People are surrounded by customs as much as by air. The circle becomes social, so environment names the culture that shapes a person.
senses.whyCN: 人既被空气包围，也被习俗包围。这个圈变成社会的，于是 environment 指塑造一个人的文化。

senses.title: Learning environment: conditions for study
senses.definition: in education, the physical and social conditions in which learning takes place
senses.definitionCN: 教育中指学习发生的物理与社会条件
senses.example: A quiet environment helps students concentrate.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的环境有助于学生集中注意力。
senses.why: Classrooms are a designed circle: lighting, noise, and relationships together set what a learner can do.
senses.whyCN: 教室是一个被设计出来的圈：灯光、噪音和人际关系共同决定学习者能做什么。

senses.title: Computing environment: the system a program runs in
senses.titleCN: 计算环境：程序运行所在的系统
senses.definition: in computing, the hardware and software conditions in which a program runs
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域指程序运行所依赖的硬件与软件条件
senses.example: The old software will not run in a 64-bit environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧软件无法在 64 位环境中运行。
senses.why: A program is surrounded by an operating system and settings; computing simply names that technical circle with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 程序被操作系统和各项设置包围；计算机领域只是用同一个词命名这个技术性的圈。

senses.title: The environment as a policy object
senses.definition: the environment, with the definite article, as the target of protection and regulation
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时，指保护与监管的对象
senses.example: The agency was created to protect the environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构是为了保护环境而设立的。
senses.why: Once the natural circle is threatened, it becomes a thing to defend; the definite article marks the shared surroundings of all people.
senses.whyCN: 一旦自然之圈受到威胁，它就变成要捍卫的对象；定冠词标记的是所有人共享的周围世界。

senses.title: Business or market environment
senses.definition: the conditions under which a company or market operates
senses.definitionCN: 公司或市场运作所处的条件
senses.example: Low interest rates created a favourable environment for startups.
senses.exampleCN: 低利率为初创企业创造了有利的环境。
senses.why: Firms are surrounded by prices, rules, and rivals. The same circle, drawn around a market, gives the business sense.
senses.whyCN: 公司被价格、规则和对手包围。把同一个圈画在市场周围，就得到商业义。

senses.title: Environment vs surroundings: the whole set, not the items
senses.titleCN: environment 与 surroundings：整体条件，而非物件清单
senses.definition: the total set of conditions, as opposed to surroundings, which stresses the nearby objects
senses.definitionCN: 条件的整体集合，与强调附近物件的 surroundings 相对
senses.example: The patient's whole environment, not just the ward, affected recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 影响病人康复的是他的整个环境，而不只是病房。
senses.why: Environment names the enclosing system as a whole; surroundings counts the things nearby. The -ment ending marks the state of being surrounded, not a list of objects.
senses.whyCN: environment 命名整个包围系统；surroundings 数的是附近的物件。-ment 词尾标记“被包围的状态”，而不是一份物件清单。

intro.en: Environment began around 1600 as 'the state of being surrounded'. It grew from the verb environ 'to surround', and only in the 19th and 20th centuries did it become the word for natural and social conditions.
intro.cn: environment 约 1600 年以“被环绕的状态”出现。它由动词 environ“环绕”生长而来，直到 19、20 世纪才成为表示自然与社会条件的词。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'state of being environed', a noun of state built on the verb environ plus -ment.
items.cn: 最早记录义为“被环绕的状态”，是由动词 environ 加 -ment 构成的状态名词。

items.en: The verb environ 'to surround, encircle' is recorded in late 14th-century English.
items.cn: 动词 environ“环绕、围住”记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语。

items.en: From Old French environer, from environ 'around' = en- 'in' + viron 'circle, circuit', from virer 'to turn'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 environer，源自 environ“周围”= en-“内”+ viron“圆圈、一圈”，后者来自 virer“转”。

items.en: The sense 'the conditions in which a person or thing lives' is recorded in 1827, when Carlyle used it to translate German Umgebung.
items.cn: “人或物所处条件的总和”这一义项记录于 1827 年，卡莱尔用它翻译德语 Umgebung。

items.en: Ecology gives 'the natural world' its modern currency from 1956, and the environmental movement spreads it further.
items.cn: 生态学从 1956 年起让“自然世界”义流行起来，环保运动又把它传播得更广。

items.en: Modern English extends environment to computing and business; the old verb survives mainly in the plural noun environs, 'the outskirts'.
items.cn: 现代英语把 environment 扩展到计算机与商业领域；旧动词主要保留在复数名词 environs“近郊”中。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the area around a town or place. It names the outskirts, not the total conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇周边的地区；近郊。它指外围地带，而不是条件的总和。

entries.definition: relating to the environment. It is the adjective formed from the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 环境的；与环境有关的。它是由该名词构成的形容词。

entries.definition: to surround, a rare formal verb. Environment is the noun built from it with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕；围住，是罕用的正式动词。environment 是它加 -ment 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the things and conditions near someone. It counts nearby objects, while environment names the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 周围的事物与条件。它数的是附近物件，而 environment 指整个系统。

entries.definition: the place or background where something happens. It is narrower and often used of stories or scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的地点或背景。它更窄，常用于故事或场景。

entries.definition: the natural home of a plant or animal. It is a biologist's term for one species' environment.
entries.definitionCN: 动植物的天然栖息地。它是生物学术语，指某一物种的环境。

entries.definition: the social and cultural background of a person or group. It is literary and almost always social.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体的社会文化背景。它偏文学，几乎总指社会层面。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: environ plus -ment, the viron 'circle' inside the word, and the surviving relatives environ, environs and environmental.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：environ + -ment、词内的 viron“圆圈”，以及仍活着的同族词 environ、environs、environmental。

normal.en: environ means 'to surround', and -ment turns the action into a state: environment is the state of being surrounded.
normal.cn: environ 意为“环绕”，-ment 把动作变成状态：environment 就是“被围住的状态”。

normal.en: viron meant 'circle, circuit' in Old French, and virer 'to turn' is the same source as English veer.
normal.cn: viron 在古法语中意为“圆圈、一圈”，而 virer“转”与英语 veer 同源。

normal.en: environs keeps the old verb alive: it means the area that circles a town.
normal.cn: environs 让旧动词继续活着：它指环绕城镇的那片外围地区。

normal.en: environmental, environmentally, environmentalist and environmentalism are the modern derivatives built on the noun.
normal.cn: environmental、environmentally、environmentalist、environmentalism 都是在这个名词上构成的现代派生词。

normal.en: the environment, with the definite article, is the shared natural circle that policy tries to protect.
normal.cn: 带定冠词的 the environment，是政策试图保护的那个共享自然之圈。

abstract.en: Draw a circle around a body: inside it put air, water, food, people and rules.
abstract.cn: 在一个身体周围画一个圈：圈里放空气、水、食物、人和规则。

abstract.en: The same circle can shrink to a classroom, a lab, or a server, and expand to the whole planet.
abstract.cn: 同一个圈可以缩小到一间教室、一间实验室或一台服务器，也可以扩大到整个星球。

abstract.en: What surrounds also shapes: the circle is not a backdrop but a set of forces acting on what lives inside.
abstract.cn: 包围者也在塑造：这个圈不是背景板，而是一组作用于圈内生命的力量。

examples.en: The desert environment is harsh for both plants and animals.
examples.cn: 沙漠环境对植物和动物都很严酷。

examples.en: She grew up in an environment where books were always available.
examples.cn: 她在书籍随手可及的环境中长大。

examples.en: The program stores its settings in an environment file.
examples.cn: 该程序把设置保存在一个环境文件里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因围门」——因为四周都围上了门，圈出一块地方 → environment 环境、周围状况

root: 源自古法语 environ“环绕”= en-“内”+ viron“圆圈”← virer“转”，核心是“围在人或物外面的一圈条件”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of environment all come from one circle drawn around a person, animal, or thing. The circle can shrink to a room or a server, or expand to the whole natural world.
sensesIntro.cn: environment 的九个义项都来自画在人、动物或事物外面的同一个圈。这个圈可以缩小到一间房或一台服务器，也可以扩大到整个自然世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle drawn around a body, holding air, water, people and rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一个身体画出的圈，圈里装着空气、水、人与规则。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE ITSELF: the state of being surrounded, and the total set of conditions around a body.
branches.cn: 圈本身：被包围的状态，以及相对于附近物件清单的整体条件。

branches.en: NATURE AND HABITAT: the planetary natural system, and the narrower conditions in which one organism lives.
branches.cn: 自然与栖息地：行星级的自然系统，以及某一生物生活的较窄条件。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND LEARNING: social and cultural surroundings where people grow and learn.
branches.cn: 人与学习：社会文化氛围，以及教室这类被设计的学习条件。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND MARKET CIRCLES: the system that a program, machine or business operates within.
branches.cn: 技术与市场之圈：程序周围的系统，以及公司周围的条件。

branches.en: POLICY: the shared natural circle that governments promise to protect.
branches.cn: 政策：共享的自然之圈变成国家保护的对象。

intro.en: Environment is en- plus viron 'circle' plus -ment, a noun of state. English builds environmental, environmentally, environmentalist and environmentalism on top, and keeps the bare verb environ.
intro.cn: environment 是 en- + viron“圆圈”+ -ment 构成的状态名词。英语在其上构成 environmental、environmentally、environmentalist、environmentalism，并保留光秃的动词 environ。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin ancestor to list. The word comes from Old French environer, and the deeper origin of viron and virer is uncertain, with only a possible link to Latin vibrare 'to shake'.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁祖先可列。这个词来自古法语 environer，viron 与 virer 的更深来源不确定，只有与拉丁语 vibrare“摇动”的可能联系。

items.meaning: the state of being surrounded; the surrounding conditions
items.meaningCN: 被环绕的状态；周围条件（-ment 构成状态名词）
items.example: A calm environment helps children learn.
items.exampleCN: 平静的环境有助于孩子学习。

items.meaningCN: 环绕；围住（罕用的正式动词）
items.example: Tall hedges environ the old garden.
items.exampleCN: 高高的树篱环绕着这座老花园。

items.meaningCN: 周边地区；近郊（-s 构成复数名词）
items.example: Many commuters live in the environs of the city.
items.exampleCN: 许多通勤者住在城市近郊。

items.meaningCN: 环境的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The report lists the main environmental risks.
items.exampleCN: 报告列出了主要的环境风险。

items.meaningCN: 在环境方面；环保地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a person who works to protect the environment
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义者（-ist 表示人）
items.example: The environmentalist opposed the new road.
items.exampleCN: 那位环保人士反对修建新公路。

items.meaning: the movement to protect the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义（-ism 表示主义、运动）
items.exampleCN: 环境保护主义在 20 世纪 70 年代迅速发展。

items.meaningCN: 突然转向（与 virer“转”同源）
items.example: The boat veered away from the rocks.
items.exampleCN: 小船突然转向，避开了礁石。

definition_zh: 没有；不带；不用；（后接动名词）不…就；在…之外
definition_en: not having, not using, or not accompanied by something, and in older use, outside of
core_image: 一个人出门时两只手都空着，口袋里什么也没装
scene: 他出门时两手空空，口袋里什么也没带，连钥匙都留在了桌上。 We cannot finish the work without more help.
sceneCN: 这里 without 是「没有」（第 1 个义项：不带、缺少某物）；句意为没有更多人手，我们完不成这项工作。两手空着出门的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 与…一起（反义）
在…之内
扣留；不给
缺乏

senses.title: Not having something
senses.definition: not having or not carrying something that is usually there
senses.definitionCN: 没有或未携带通常应存在之物
senses.example: We cannot finish the work without more help.
senses.exampleCN: 没有更多人手，我们完不成这项工作。
senses.why: The oldest form meant outside of, and what is outside you is simply not yours to hold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的形式意为在…之外，而在你之外的东西就不在你手里。

senses.title: Not using something
senses.definition: not using a thing, or not doing something, as in without a key or without asking
senses.definitionCN: 不使用某物，或不做某事，如不用钥匙、不打招呼
senses.example: He opened the lock without a key.
senses.exampleCN: 他没用钥匙就把锁打开了。
senses.why: Doing something without a tool means the tool is outside the act, which is the same picture again.
senses.whyCN: 不使用工具做事，意味着工具在这一动作之外，又是同一幅画面。

senses.title: Not accompanied by
senses.definition: with no one or nothing else present, in phrases such as without a word
senses.definitionCN: 没有其他人在场或没有别的东西相伴，如 without a word
senses.example: She left the room without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一句话没说就离开了房间。
senses.why: A companion who is outside the scene is absent, so the preposition also marks silent or lonely action.
senses.whyCN: 不在场景里的同伴就是缺席，所以这个介词也能标记沉默或孤单的行动。

senses.title: Outside of, in older use
senses.definition: in old or literary style, on the outside of a place
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式或文学文体中，指在某地之外
senses.example: Without the city walls lay a wide empty field.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙之外是一片开阔的空地。
senses.why: This is the original sense, still alive in poetry, from which all the others grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是最原始的义项，仍活在诗歌里，其余义项都由它生长出来。

intro.en: Without began as with plus out, meaning outside, and only later slid into the modern sense of not having.
intro.cn: without 起初是 with 加 out，意为在外，后来才滑向现代「没有」的义项。

items.en: wiðutan meant outside, on the outer side of a place or a group.
items.cn: wiðutan 意为在外，处于某地或某群之外。

items.en: Being outside a group meant being denied what the group had.
items.cn: 处在群体之外，就意味着得不到群体拥有的东西。

items.en: The form became without and the lack sense came forward.
items.cn: 形式变作 without，缺少义走到了前面。

items.en: The outside sense narrowed to literary use, and the lack sense took over daily speech.
items.cn: 在外义收窄到文学用法，缺少义占领了日常言语。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as without doubt and without delay made the preposition essential.
items.cn: without doubt、without delay 这类固定短语让这个介词必不可少。

note.en: The first group collects the with family, the second other ways to say a thing is missing.
note.cn: 第一组收 with 家族，第二组收其他表示「缺失」的说法。

normalIntro.en: Without is with plus out, so its oldest picture is simply being out of something, not having it.
normalIntro.cn: without 是 with 加 out，最古老的画面就是身在某物之外，因而没有它。

normal.en: With plus out: to be out of a thing is to be without it.
normal.cn: with 加 out：在东西之外，就是没有它。

normal.en: The th is voiced, as in this; the ending out is clear.
normal.cn: th 是浊音，与 this 相同；结尾的 out 很清楚。

normal.en: The tip is flat on the upper teeth, the same shape as within.
normal.cn: 舌尖平贴上齿，与 within 一样。

normal.en: You cannot do without water: the phrase do without means manage anyway.
normal.cn: cannot do without water 意为离不开水；do without 意为将就着也行。

normal.en: Without doubt and without delay are fixed pairs worth learning as blocks.
normal.cn: without doubt 与 without delay 都是值得整块记下的固定搭配。

abstract.en: Two empty hands turned palm up.
abstract.cn: 两只空空的手，掌心朝上。

abstract.en: A table set for one instead of two.
abstract.cn: 一人份而非两人份的餐具。

abstract.en: A door closing on the sound of footsteps, and then silence.
abstract.cn: 门在脚步声之后关上，然后是安静。

examples.en: She cannot read without her glasses.
examples.cn: 不戴眼镜她看不了书。

examples.en: He agreed without asking what it would cost.
examples.cn: 他还没问要花多少钱就答应了。

examples.en: Without water, the garden would die in a week.
examples.cn: 没有水，这园子一周就会枯掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: with + out —— 东西在范围之外，自然就是「没有」。

root: 古英语 wið + utan（with + out，在外）→ wiðutan → without；反义形式有 with、within。

sensesIntro.en: From being outside a group, the word comes to mean lacking a thing, not using it, not being accompanied by it, and keeps the old sense of outside in poetry.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从身处群体之外，变成缺少某物、不使用某物、无人相伴，并在诗里保留着「在外」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two empty hands, palms turned up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只空手，掌心朝上。

branches.en: The lack branch: no extra help to finish the work.
branches.cn: 缺少分支：没有更多人手完成工作。

branches.en: The unused tool branch: a lock opened with no key.
branches.cn: 不用工具分支：不用钥匙打开的锁。

branches.en: The alone branch: leaving the room wordless.
branches.cn: 孤单分支：没说一句话就离开房间。

branches.en: The old branch: fields lying outside the walls.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：城墙外的空地。

branches.en: The negation branch: what is absent shapes what remains.
branches.cn: 否定分支：缺席之物塑造了其余的处境。

intro.en: Without is a fused pair, with plus out, and its mirror word is within.
intro.cn: without 是 with 与 out 熔成的一对，它的镜像词是 within。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin entries below are the usual borrowed ways to express lack.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于日耳曼语；下面的拉丁条目是表达缺失的常见借入方式。

items.example: The first half of the compound.
The half that turns the word negative.
items.exampleCN: 让这个词带否定的后半。

items.example: A suffix with the same force.

items.exampleCN: 另一种表达缺席的方式。

items.example: The lack turned into an action.
A fixed block of everyday speech.

definition_zh: 绳；绳索；诀窍；用绳捆
definition_en: a strong thick cord, the skills needed for a job, or to tie something with a rope
core_image: 盘在甲板上的粗绳
scene: 登山者把绳子牢牢系在岩石上。 The climber tied the rope firmly to the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 rope 是「绳索」（第 1 个义项）；句意：登山者把绳子牢牢系在岩石上。

derivatives.zh: 绳状的；黏稠的
制绳者；套索者
用绳围隔

senses.title: Strong cord
senses.definition: a strong thick cord made of twisted threads
senses.definitionCN: 由多股线拧成的结实粗绳
senses.example: The boat was tied with a thick rope.
senses.exampleCN: 船用一根粗绳系住了。
senses.why: Twisted threads make one strong line.
senses.whyCN: 拧在一起的线形成一根结实的绳。

senses.title: Know-how
senses.definition: the skills and knowledge needed for a job
senses.definitionCN: 从事某项工作所需的技能与知识
senses.example: It took a month to learn the ropes.
senses.exampleCN: 熟悉门道花了一个月。
senses.why: A sailor must know every rope on the ship.
senses.whyCN: 水手必须认识船上的每一根绳。

senses.title: Tie or fence
senses.definition: to tie something with a rope or keep people back with one
senses.definitionCN: 用绳子捆住某物，或用绳子把人隔开
senses.example: Police roped off the narrow lane.
senses.exampleCN: 警察用绳子把窄巷隔开。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of using the cord.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成使用绳索的动作。

intro.en: Rope comes from Old English rap, a strong cord.
intro.cn: rope 源自古代英语 rap，意为结实的绳。

items.en: Rap names a strong twisted cord.
items.cn: rap 指结实的拧绳。

items.en: Related forms name a cord in other northern tongues.
items.cn: 其他北方语言中的相关形式也指绳索。

items.en: Rope becomes the standard spelling.
items.cn: rope 成为标准拼写。

items.en: Sailors learn the ropes of a ship.
items.cn: 水手要熟悉船上的绳索。

items.en: Learn the ropes comes to mean know-how.
items.cn: learn the ropes 转指掌握门道。

note.en: A rope is thick; a robe is clothing.
note.cn: rope 是粗绳，robe 则是长袍。

entries.definition: a long loose garment
a wish for a good result
like a rope or sticky
a thin strong string
a long thin cord
a thick strong wire or rope

normalIntro.en: Rope ties things, and knowing your ropes means knowing the job.
normalIntro.cn: rope 把东西系住，熟悉绳索则意味着熟悉工作。

normal.en: He tied the boat with a heavy rope.
normal.cn: 他用一根粗绳把船系好。

normal.en: The children played with a jump rope.
normal.cn: 孩子们玩跳绳。

normal.en: They climbed down a rope ladder.
normal.cn: 他们顺着绳梯爬下去。

normal.en: Workers roped off the wet floor.
normal.cn: 工人用绳子把湿滑地面隔开。

normal.en: It takes time to learn the ropes.
normal.cn: 熟悉门道需要时间。

abstract.en: Picture a coil of rope on a wooden deck.
abstract.cn: 想象木甲板上盘着的一卷绳。

abstract.en: Imagine many threads twisting into one strong line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多细线拧成一根结实的绳。

abstract.en: Think of a rope barrier holding a crowd back.
abstract.cn: 想象一道绳栏把人群挡在后面。

examples.en: The rescue team threw a rope to the swimmer.
examples.cn: 救援队把绳子抛给游泳者。

examples.en: She learned the ropes of the new job quickly.
examples.cn: 她很快熟悉了新工作的门道。

examples.en: The garden was roped off for repairs.
examples.cn: 花园因维修被绳子围了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rope」像「绕」——许多细线绕在一起，就成了结实的绳索。

root: 古代英语 rap（结实的绳索），核心义「多股拧成、用于系绑的长索」。

sensesIntro.en: Rope means a strong thick cord, the know-how for a job, or to tie or fence with a cord.
sensesIntro.cn: rope 意为结实粗绳、工作中的门道，或用绳捆扎与围隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coil of rope on a deck.
core.cn: 核心意象：甲板上盘着的一卷绳。

branches.en: The strong cord is the main sense.
branches.cn: 结实绳索是主要义项。

branches.en: Knowing the ropes means knowing the job.
branches.cn: 熟悉绳索就是熟悉工作。

branches.en: The verb puts the cord to use.
branches.cn: 动词把绳索用于行动。

branches.en: Cord and tying belong together.
branches.cn: 绳索与系绑密不可分。

branches.en: The sailor image links tool and skill.
branches.cn: 水手形象连接了工具与技能。

intro.en: Rope is an Old English word with a small English family.
intro.cn: rope 是古代英语词，有一个小小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Rope has no Latin root; its history is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: rope 没有拉丁词根，其历史属于日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 形式；形状；表格；种类；形成；组成；养成
definition_en: the shape or type of something; a printed document with spaces to fill in; to make or begin to have a shape
core_image: 一团泥被捏出轮廓：无形的东西获得确定的形状
scene: 开学第一天，老师发下一张纸，让每个人填写姓名和班级。 Please fill in this form with your name and class.
sceneCN: 这里 form 是「表格」的意思（第 3 个义项：需要填写的文件）；开学时人人都要填一张登记表。

derivatives.zh: form 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「正式的；外表的」
form 加 -ation，义为「形成；编队；构造」
义为「以前的；前者」，来自 form 的比较级形态
同根词，义为「公式；配方」
加前缀 re-，义为「改革；改良」
加前缀 in-，义为「告知；使成形于心中」

senses.title: The visible shape of something
senses.definition: the visible shape or outline of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或物可见的轮廓和形状。
senses.example: In the fog we could see the form of a tall building.
senses.exampleCN: 雾中我们只能看到一座高楼的轮廓。
senses.why: The Latin root forma names shape itself, before any abstract use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 forma 最初命名的是形状本身，先于一切抽象用法。

senses.title: A type or kind of something
senses.definition: a type or variety of something, especially in abstract contexts
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的类型或存在方式，尤用于抽象语境。
senses.example: Email is now a common form of communication.
senses.exampleCN: 电子邮件如今是常见的交流形式。
senses.why: Visible shape extends to the 'shape' of abstract things like activities or energy.
senses.whyCN: 可见的形状延伸到抽象事物的「形状」，比如活动或能量的形态。

senses.title: A printed document with blanks
senses.definition: a printed paper or web page with empty spaces for writing information
senses.definitionCN: 印有空白栏、供人填写信息的纸页或网页。
senses.example: Please fill in this form and sign at the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 请填写这张表格并在底部签名。
senses.why: A form gives information a fixed shape, like a mold.
senses.whyCN: 表格给信息规定固定形状，像模具一样。

senses.title: To make, build, or begin to exist
senses.definition: to give something a shape, or to start to exist as a group or thing
senses.definitionCN: 使某物具有形状，或（群体、事物）开始形成。
senses.example: The students formed a line at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在校门口排成一列。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to produce form.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：去「制造」形状。

senses.title: To develop a habit or idea gradually
senses.definition: to develop a habit, idea, or judgement over time
senses.definitionCN: 习惯、想法或判断随着时间慢慢养成。
senses.example: Reading before bed helped her form good habits.
senses.exampleCN: 睡前阅读帮助她养成好习惯。
senses.why: Abstract forming happens slowly, as shapes emerge in nature.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「形成」是缓慢发生的，正如自然界中形状的浮现。

intro.en: Form comes straight from Latin forma, one of the most productive roots in English.
intro.cn: form 直接来自拉丁语 forma，是英语中能产性最强的词根之一。

items.en: Forma meant shape, figure, or appearance, and also a mold or pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 forma 意为形状、轮廓、外貌，也指模具、样板。

items.en: A related root *dher- meant to hold or support, giving the sense of a fixed outline.
items.cn: 相关词根 *dher- 意为「持有、支撑」，引出「固定轮廓」的意味（重构形式）。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as forme in learned and everyday use.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语写作 forme，用于书面与日常。

items.en: English borrowed forme around the twelfth to thirteenth century in the shape sense.
items.cn: 英语在十二至十三世纪借入 forme，先表示形状。

items.en: The document sense, the verb uses, and the huge derived family all flourished in Modern English.
items.cn: 「表格」义、动词用法和庞大的派生词族都在现代英语中蓬勃发展。

note.en: Words that look like form and words about shape, type, and making.
note.cn: 与 form 形近的词，以及表示形状、种类、塑造的词。

entries.definition: an eating tool; differs from form by one final letter
entries.definitionCN: 叉子；与 form 仅词尾一字母之差。

entries.definition: a company, or solid and steady; a frequent confusion with form
entries.definitionCN: 公司；坚固的；与 form 极易混淆，注意元音不同。

entries.definition: starting point of movement; differs by one letter and position
entries.definitionCN: 从、来自；与 form 字母相同仅序不同，拼写陷阱词。

entries.definition: the outline or form of something
entries.definitionCN: 形状；与 form 的第 1 义项近义，更口语。

entries.definition: the way parts are arranged into a whole
entries.definitionCN: 结构；强调部分之间的组织。

entries.definition: a visible shape, especially of a body
entries.definitionCN: 轮廓；体型；与 form 的外形义相近。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks connecting form's shape core to its main uses.
normalIntro.cn: 把 form 的「形状」核心与主要用法连起来的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Forma in Latin means shape: every sense is a kind of shaping.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 forma 就是「形状」：每个义项都是某种「塑形」。

normal.en: A form of water is ice, liquid, or steam: three shapes of one thing.
normal.cn: 水的形式是冰、液、汽：同一事物的三种形态。

normal.en: A form on paper gives blanks their fixed shape.
normal.cn: 纸上的表格给空白规定了固定的形状。

normal.en: Form a line at school: people take the shape of a queue.
normal.cn: form a line：人排成队列的形状。

normal.en: Watch the trap pair: form (shape) versus from (source).
normal.cn: 注意易混对：form（形状）与 from（来自）。

abstract.en: Picture wet clay taking shape on a spinning wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象湿泥在转轮上渐渐现出轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture ice cubes freezing into square forms.
abstract.cn: 想象水冻成正方体的冰块。

abstract.en: Picture scattered students forming a neat line.
abstract.cn: 想象散乱的学生排成整齐的一列。

examples.en: Fill in the form and hand it back to me today.
examples.cn: 填好这张表格，今天交回给我。

examples.en: Water can exist in the form of ice, liquid, and steam.
examples.cn: 水可以以冰、液体和水蒸气的形式存在。

examples.en: The two countries formed a new trade partnership.
examples.cn: 两国组成了新的贸易伙伴关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛母」——佛母孕育形貌，众生皆有形：form 就是一切事物的「形」。

root: form 来自拉丁语 forma（形状、轮廓、模具），一般认为与词根 *dher-（持有、支撑）相关（重构形式）。经古法语 forme 进入中古英语。「形状→种类→表格→塑形动词」全部由「形」这一核心辐射。

sensesIntro.en: Form runs from visible shape to abstract type, to documents, to verbs of making.
sensesIntro.cn: form 从可见形状走向抽象种类，再到文书表格，最后成为「塑造」类动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shapeless matter taking on a definite outline
core.cn: 核心意象：无形之物获得确定的轮廓

branches.en: The outline a body shows to the eye
branches.cn: 肉眼看到的轮廓外形

branches.en: The shape of abstract things such as energy
branches.cn: 抽象事物（如能量）的形态

branches.en: A mold that gives written information a shape
branches.cn: 给书面信息塑形的模具，即表格

branches.en: Giving shape to things and groups
branches.cn: 给事物、群体赋予形状的动作

branches.en: Slow shaping inside habits and opinions
branches.cn: 在习惯与观点中缓慢进行的塑形

intro.en: Form is one of the most fertile Latin roots in English, spawning a whole family.
intro.cn: form 是英语中最高产的拉丁词根之一，孕育了庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forma and its relatives supply both English derivatives and Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma 及其近亲既供给了英语派生词，也留下了拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fog hid the form of the tower.

items.exampleCN: 「有固定外形」引申为「讲究场合」。
in- 在此不表否定词义之外的反义。

items.meaning: the act or result of forming
items.exampleCN: 名词化：塑造的过程或结果。
trans-（穿过）+ 塑形 = 彻底改形。

items.meaning: one shape for all; same everywhere

items.exampleCN: forma 的小词形：「固定的小模子」。

items.example: The formative years of a child.

definition_zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言
definition_en: to make the sound of a word or letter, or to announce something formally and officially
core_image: 嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一串字母变成别人听得见的声音
scene: 新生点名时，老师把花名册上的名字一个个念出来，念到某个姓氏时停了一下。 She paused to pronounce the unfamiliar surname slowly and clearly.
sceneCN: 这里取「发音、读出来」的意思（第 1 个义项：把词或字母读出声音）；句意为她停下来，把这个不常见的姓氏慢慢地、清楚地读了出来。花名册上那个生僻的姓就是线索。

pos.zh: 发音；读作；宣判；正式宣布；断言

derivatives.zh: 由 pronounce 加 -ment 构成，义为「公告；正式声明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「明显的；显著的」
由同一拉丁词干的名词 pronuntiatio 经法语进入英语，义为「发音」
在 pronounce 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错」

senses.title: To make the sound of a word or letter
senses.definition: to make the sound of a word, a name or a letter with the voice
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音发出单词、名字或字母的读音
senses.example: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
senses.exampleCN: 班上没人能读出她的姓。
senses.why: Latin nuntiare meant to announce, and pro- meant forth, so the pair first meant to bring a sound out into the open; the mouth is only the instrument that does it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nuntiare 意为「宣告」，前缀 pro- 意为「向外」，两者合起来本是「把声音送到外面」；嘴巴只是完成这件事的工具，不是词义的起点。

senses.title: To declare something officially
senses.definition: to announce a sentence, a verdict or a decision in a formal and official way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、官方的方式宣布判决、裁定或决定
senses.example: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 法官宣判五年徒刑。
senses.why: A court does not merely think its decision, it says it aloud, and the announcing half of the Latin word survives exactly there: the sentence takes effect when it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判决不只是想清楚，还要念出来；拉丁词里「宣告」的那一半正好留在这种场合——判词被说出口的那一刻才生效。

senses.title: To state an opinion firmly
senses.definition: to give a firm opinion or judgement about something, often in a slightly formal tone
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给出明确而坚定的看法或评判，语气常偏正式
senses.example: The critic pronounced the film a masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 那位影评人断言这部电影是杰作。
senses.why: Anyone who announces a verdict is borrowing a judge's authority, so the word widened from courtrooms to critics and experts who speak as if their view were a ruling.
senses.whyCN: 宣告裁定的人都在借用法官的权威，于是这个词从法庭扩展到评论家和专家身上——他们说话时，仿佛自己的看法就是一条裁定。

senses.title: To be sounded in a particular way
senses.definition: to be sounded in the way described, said of a written word, a name or a letter
senses.definitionCN: 读音如所说的那样，用于说明写出来的单词、名字或字母怎么念
senses.example: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。
senses.why: English spelling and sound often part company, so the same verb is used passively to record how a written form is actually said, with no declaring involved at all.
senses.whyCN: 英语的拼写和读音常常对不上，于是同一个动词也用被动形式来记录「写出来的形式实际怎么念」，此时完全与「宣告」无关。

intro.en: Pronounce joins a Latin prefix meaning forth to a Latin verb meaning to announce, so the word has always carried both a mouth and a public voice.
intro.cn: pronounce 把表示「向外」的拉丁语前缀接在表示「宣告」的拉丁语动词上，所以这个词从源头起就同时带着「嘴」和「公开的声音」。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce, to report or to bring news, and the related noun nuntius meant messenger.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告、带来消息，相关名词 nuntius 指信使。

items.en: Adding pro-, forth, produced pronuntiare, to speak out, to utter, and already to declare in public.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的 pro-，得到 pronuntiare，意为说出、发声，并且已经带有「当众宣告」的意味。

items.en: The action noun pronuntiatio named a speaking out and a declaration, and it is the ancestor of the English noun.
items.cn: 动作名词 pronuntiatio 指「说出」与「宣告」，它是英语名词 pronunciation 的祖先。

items.en: Old French softened the consonant cluster and gave the verb as prononcier, with the o of the Latin noun but no t before the ending.
items.cn: 古法语把辅音簇软化，动词写作 prononcier，保有拉丁名词里的 o，但词尾前没有 t。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as pronounce and used it for sounding words and for formal declarations; the noun came separately from the Latin noun, which is why pronunciation has no o.
items.cn: 中古英语借入动词作 pronounce，既用于读词，也用于正式宣告；名词则另从拉丁名词借入，所以 pronunciation 里没有 o。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb for announcing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for producing words with the voice.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「宣告」动词上的形式；近义组收用嗓音说出词语的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the way a word is spoken, with no o after the n.
entries.definitionCN: 表示词的读法的名词，n 后面没有 o。

entries.definition: A formal public statement or declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明或宣告。

entries.definition: To say a word in a wrong way.
To make something known publicly.
To say words clearly and distinctly.
To say something aloud.
To form sounds clearly enough to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 把音发清楚，使人听得懂。

entries.definition: To state something officially or firmly.
To produce words with the voice.

normalIntro.en: The word holds a mouth and a public voice at once, and its family keeps splitting along those two lines: sounding words, and declaring things.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时握着「嘴」和「公开的声音」，同族词也沿这两条线分开：读词，以及宣告。

normal.en: Latin nuntiare also gives announce, so pronounce and announce are cousins: both bring something out where others can hear it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare 也带来 announce，所以 pronounce 与 announce 是表亲：两者都把东西送到别人听得见的地方。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means forth, so to pronounce is literally to carry a sound out of the mouth.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「向外」，所以 pronounce 字面上就是「把声音从嘴里送出去」。

normal.en: The noun pronunciation comes from Latin pronuntiatio, not from the English verb, which is why the o of pronounce is missing there.
normal.cn: 名词 pronunciation 来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，而不是来自英语动词，所以那里少了 pronounce 的 o。

normal.en: The adjective pronounced means noticeable, because something pronounced has been said out clearly enough to be heard.
normal.cn: 形容词 pronounced 意为「明显的」，因为被清楚说出来的东西自然引人注意。

normal.en: A judge pronounces sentence: the legal use draws on the announcing half of the word, not on the mouth.
normal.cn: 法官宣判用 pronounce sentence，这个法律用法取的是词里「宣告」的那一半，与嘴无关。

abstract.en: A word only becomes fully real when someone pronounces it; print is little more than a set of instructions for the mouth.
abstract.cn: 一个词只有被人念出来才完全成立；纸上的拼写不过是给嘴巴的一套说明。

abstract.en: Saying a verdict and saying a word share one verb because both make something official simply by speaking it.
abstract.cn: 宣读判决和读出一个词共用一个动词，因为两者都只靠「说出来」就让某事生效。

abstract.en: The distance between how a word is written and how it is pronounced is where the history of the language shows through.
abstract.cn: 一个词「怎么写」和「怎么念」之间的距离，正是这门语言的历史露出来的地方。

examples.en: Nobody in the class could pronounce her family name.
examples.cn: 班上没人能读出她的姓。

examples.en: The judge pronounced a sentence of five years.
examples.cn: 法官宣判五年徒刑。

examples.en: The town's name is pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
examples.cn: 这个镇的名字重音落在第一个音节上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若闹恩斯」——像「扑上去念」，凑到字母跟前使劲念，就是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，本义「说出、当众宣告」；动词经古法语 prononcier 进入英语作 pronounce，名词则另从拉丁语 pronuntiatio 借入。

sensesIntro.en: The core is sending a sound outward; from it grow the mouth's work of saying words, the courtroom's spoken verdict, the expert's spoken judgement, and the passive record of how a written form sounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把声音送出去」；由它长出嘴读词的动作、法庭上念出的判词、专家说出的定论，以及被动记录「写出来的形式怎么念」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips, tongue and breath turning a line of printed letters into sound that other people can hear.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇、舌头和气流一起，把纸上一行字母变成别人听得见的声音。

branches.en: a teacher pointing at one letter on the board
branches.cn: 老师指着黑板上的一个字母

branches.en: a name written one way and said another
branches.cn: 写法一种、读法另一种的名字

branches.en: a courtroom where the sentence is read aloud
branches.cn: 宣读判词的法庭

branches.en: a critic closing a programme with a verdict
branches.cn: 影评人用一句定论结束节目

branches.en: words spoken as if they were final
branches.cn: 说得像终审一样的话

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and a Latin verb of announcing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示宣告的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, and its compound pronuntiare, to speak out, are the direct sources of the English verb and of its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）及其复合形式 pronuntiare（说出）是英语动词与名词的直接来源。

senses.title: The article before a vowel
senses.titleCN: 元音音素前的不定冠词
senses.definition: the form of a used before a word that begins with a vowel sound
senses.definitionCN: 用在以元音音素开头的词前的不定冠词形式
senses.example: She ate an apple after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 她午饭后吃了一个苹果。
senses.why: An is the older shape of a, kept before vowel sounds, and it still means one rather than a specific one.
senses.whyCN: an 是 a 在元音音素前保留的较早形状，仍表示「一个」而不是特指。

senses.title: Every, in a rate
senses.definition: used before a unit to mean each
senses.definitionCN: 用在单位名词前，表示每一个
senses.example: She earns ten pounds an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她每小时挣十英镑。
senses.why: One unit counted again and again becomes the rate sense of every.
senses.whyCN: 把一个单位反复数下去，就成了表示比率的「每一」。

intro.en: The recorded history of an is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 an 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: An was the old word for one, used before any noun.
items.cn: an 是古英语表示「一」的词，可用在任何名词前。

items.en: Before consonants the n was dropped, which gave the shorter form a.
items.cn: 在辅音前，n 被省去，于是有了较短的形式 a。

items.en: Before vowel sounds, an was kept because it was easier to say.
items.cn: 在元音音素前保留 an，因为这样更容易读。

items.en: English fixed the two forms by sound rather than by spelling.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪按读音而不是拼写固定了这两种形式。

items.en: Today the choice depends on the first sound of the next word.
items.cn: 今天用哪一种取决于后一个词的首音。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

normal.en: An and a are one word in two shapes: both mean one, not a particular one.
normal.cn: an 与 a 是同一个词的两种形状：都表示一个，而非特定的那个。

normal.en: The same family also gives a and one.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 a 与 one。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase an apple.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「一个苹果」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of an in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 an 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: the form of a used before a vowel sound, or before a unit to mean every.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「一个（元音音素前）」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a single apple lying on a table.

abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。
